Keep MingToon Manager on the root of every avatar you work on with MingToon. It manages target meshes, conversion, looks, and update checks. This guide starts with adding Manager after installation, then converting and refining materials in Quick Settings. Complete installation first. Face SDF Studio is not yet released and is not needed for this workflow.
Join the Open Beta

Purpose: Apply one value to several MingToon materials, or save and reuse a look preset. The first action is to open Bulk Settings, choose a scope and filters, and check Preview Material Count.

Base colour, surface mode and the everyday maps - the first things you touch on a new material.
Controls that treat the face and the whole character as their own thing. Assign face and skin roles before adjusting their effects.
Screen-space effects that read the camera depth texture. Without depth they vanish entirely, so confirm depth before touching any value here. Inner 2D Edge lives in this group too.
The layers and material response stacked on the base. Every layered section shares one trap: a slot past the layer count is skipped entirely.
The single biggest lever on a toon look. Form Shadow (light-direction shading) and Shadow Projection (real-time cast shadow) are separate sections - keep them apart.
Normal Outline expands the mesh, so it does not require camera depth. Inner 2D Edge, which reads screen depth to draw lines inside the surface, lives in the Depth Effects group.
This group lifts the silhouette and separates the character from the background. They stack fast, so raise one at a time.

A character toon shader connecting facial shading, clothing detail, and silhouette. MingToon brings together the direction of facial shadows, the way light and shadow overlap, and the colour and texture of surfaces. Build the face, hair, and clothing material by material, then use MingToon Manager to adjust the look across the avatar. Start with MingToon Manager · Start with installation · Convert a lilToon avatar · Check current limitations Current public version: 0.1.10 BRP Open Beta The current download is the Built-in Render Pipeline (BRP) core beta. Check the installation guide for the environment required by VRChat, Warudo, or general Unity use. VRChat client behaviour and successful upload are still being verified. Commercial use of the current Open Beta is prohibited. Join the Open Beta · BOOTH product · Licenses and included tools

Add the component → assign Face Mesh and Skin Mesh → choose a look → choose colours or existing values → convert → Quick Settings. Keep Manager on the avatar root. After editing, uploading through VRC SDK or building the WARUDO mod automatically runs optimization baking. Follow the steps. Always keep Manager on the avatar root, including when editing its outfit. Use Manager to check updates too. If installed through VCC, update MingToon in VCC. Check the installation method before following update guidance in Manager. Leave face and skin roles empty when the outfit has neither.

documents.t: Combine form shadows from surface curvature, cast shadows from real-time lights, and 2D shadows that read camera depth. Shape shading around bangs, hands, and sleeves, then use unified shadow controls to adjust the colour of overlapping areas. Overall shadow brightness and colour controls are also available. The same camera depth supports 2D rim light, inner 2D edges, depth translucency, and SSAO. These handle silhouettes, internal edges, light through thin areas, and contact darkening respectively. These effects require available camera depth. If they are missing, check the depth setup and target environment first. Some environments may require a depth-enabling assist light. → Light and Shadow · Depth Effects and requirements
documents.s: Control colour and edges where shadows overlap

documents.t: Texture, normal, and Matcap layers use masks to separate their areas of influence. Set up skin colour, hair highlights, and clothing patterns independently, then add hybrid PBR, toon specular, glitter, or emission where needed. Colour correction and overall brightness and tint controls help bring several materials into the same mood. Shadow patterns create halftone or line-work effects, with patterns attached to the surface or fixed to the screen. Finish the silhouette with outline and rim controls. → Detail Maps · Shadow Pattern · Outline · Rim

Combine the features needed while authoring the look. Supported build optimization paths analyze feature usage and animation dependencies to generate shaders that retain the required features. Baking separates colour information that can be stored in textures from responses that must continue to react to lighting and the view. Actual cost and results depend on the retained features, avatar, and world. Check appearance and required animations after optimization. Verified GPU performance figures are not currently published. → Automatic Optimization On Build · Shader Structure
documents.s: Carry edited materials into a build configuration

documents.t: Face SDF Studio is not yet released and is not required for this onboarding. The BRP core handles material rendering and settings. URP is excluded from the current BRP Open Beta and included with every commercial license. See Add-ons for authoring tools such as Face SDF Studio and Mask Maker. Ming Light Controller (MLC) is installed separately. It applies to an upload clone and connects virtual light, brightness, and colour controls to VRChat expression menus. The Modular Avatar path is designed to preserve existing menus, parameters, and FX; successful client upload is still being verified. MLC is included in the Personal Streaming and Personal Creator Early Access Founders Editions, and contents may change after full release. → Ming Light Controller · Licenses and included tools

MingToon connects public graphics techniques and adapted implementations to its layer, face, depth-effect, and build structures. See Third-Party Credits and Licenses for the adapted scope, original copyright, and licenses, including selected lilToon UV, colour-correction, and glitter calculations and selected NonToon shadow processing.

Situation Document I want to use it on a VRChat avatar VRChat Start creating a look Basics → Light and Shadow Migrate an existing lilToon avatar lilToon Conversion Upload an avatar Automatic Optimization On Build 2D rim light · 2D shadow not showing Depth Effects Find the meaning of one property Property Reference Something is wrong Troubleshooting Want to understand why it works that way Internal Architecture

Guides are organized by task, and references group related inspector controls. Display mode and installed add-ons can change visible groups or control locations; use inspector search as well. Inspector Group Document Basic Basics · Reference Light & Shadow Light & Shadow · Reference Rim Rim · Reference Depth Effects Depth Effects · Reference Detail Maps Detail Maps · Reference Character Character · Reference Outline Outline · Reference Reference is generated from source Property names and descriptions are taken exactly as MingToon inspector displays them. Terminology never drifts between documentation and screen.

This distribution is preview No validated GPU performance numbers are published. VRChat / Warudo are test targets and have not completed release certification. Check current limitations and release before deployment. Report bugs in the bug-report channel of the official Discord server. When reporting, including these speeds up reproduction: Unity version and target platform (VRChat PC / Warudo / general Unity) Render pipeline (BRP / URP 12.x) MingToon version (shown on the badge at the top right) Full Console log Steps to reproduce
Open Beta · September 14, 2026

Shader and bake processing, the inspector, and texture and layer editing have all been improved. A planar mode was added to the face proxy, and face-shadow adjustment, lilToon conversion, and build processing were reorganized. Factory presets were updated as well. This release is the BRP core. It supports Unity 2021.3 / 2022.3 LTS. The URP add-on and Ming Light Controller are not included. The existing Open Beta terms remain unchanged.

Less repeated work — Reusable lighting, normal, and tangent calculations are shared during baking, while unused static calculations and shader paths are reduced. Lighter outline path — Complex outline lighting and unnecessary branches were simplified. Check outline brightness and color on existing materials after updating. Separate bake modes — Choose FastUpload or Legacy GPU Precision separately for build/upload and manual bake. Select the same mode in both places when comparing the editor preview with the uploaded result. Better reuse of generated results — Generated results are reused when material, texture, mesh, and animation inputs are the same, reducing accidental reuse of stale results when inputs differ. More reliable restoration — Restoration of editable materials, keywords, and meshes after a build or bake, including cancellation and failure recovery, was strengthened. The improvement varies with material composition, rendering conditions, and cache state. This release does not turn the change into a fixed FPS or GPU improvement rate that applies to every avatar.

Consistent layout — Section headers, the top navigation area, cards, buttons, and spacing were reorganized to improve readability in a narrow inspector. Clearer performance cost display — Cost indicators in the top and sticky areas now use a consistent presentation, with more compact gauges, percentages, and details. They are estimated costs for the selected features, not actual GPU occupancy. Presets and color organization — Quick application and save/management areas now follow the same layout. A problem where color presets also overwrote the Shadow Color Map UV setting was fixed. Master adjustments — Use Overall Saturation and Overall Emission Strength to adjust the related output in one place. Rim Shade color — The Rim Shade color can be adjusted independently. At zero separate-color blending, it uses the existing shadow color. Factory preset update — Common, Face, and Skin factory presets for Basic, Hard, and Soft Toon were updated, and the High/Low display was organized. Labels and tooltips — Korean, English, and Japanese display strings, long labels, and duplicated descriptions were cleaned up.

Texture list organization — Textures can be grouped by section or sorted by GPU memory, resolution, or name. The expand-details button is placed at the far right of the card. Batch import settings — Choose Max Size, PC format, and compression quality by type for main, normal, AO, MatCap, mask, and alpha-mask textures. This changes the original textures' import settings, so it also affects other materials that share the same texture. Quick large preview — Rest the pointer on a texture for about 0.3 seconds to open a large preview. The preview closes when the pointer leaves. Better texture browsing — Folders indicate whether they contain textures, and folders with textures are ordered so they are easier to find. X/Y linking — Tiling and Offset have X/Y link buttons and a wider drag area for placement controls. Edit inside cards — Previews, color and blending, UV, channels, and adjustment controls are grouped inside cards, reducing repeated rows. Unified mask cards — Mask previews, strength, UV, inversion, channels, and detailed settings can be adjusted in one place. Mask adjustment — Supported slots expose Contrast, Blur, Input Levels, Hue, Saturation, Value, and Gamma. Input Levels can be changed with bar handles or numeric fields. Channel selection — Choose R / G / B / A / Luma with buttons. MatCap masks also offer RGB. Card reset — The card header can reset its connected texture, color, and blend settings together. AO card organization — Edit AO (Occlusion) and its strength in the texture card, then adjust Contrast, Blur, and Input Levels in the card details. The result still depends on the authored map and material settings.

Add, move, and delete — Texture, normal, and MatCap layers have add controls plus individual move and delete controls. Turn off while keeping values — A layer can be disabled and re-enabled without deleting it. When enabled again, it uses its saved texture, color, and blend settings. Animation links — Connected animations are checked before a layer is moved or deleted, and matching curves are handled with the edit. Material and curve changes can be undone together. Review the guidance when a link cannot be confirmed or when the layer count itself is animated. Color-only layers — Color-only layers that have no texture but use color and masks are handled by the conversion path.

Planar proxy added — A Plane option was added as the default face-proxy shape. Use it when aligning face-area shading to a flat, front-facing reference. Experimental shapes marked — The existing sphere, cylinder, and capsule shapes remain available as experimental shapes. Related controls grouped — The proxy shape, normal strength, normal-map influence, and related settings are placed closer together. Receiver pushback moved — Receiver Depth Pushback was moved from 2D Shadow to Face Shading. When 2D Shadow is enabled, it pushes the recorded depth and receiver surface back together to reduce depth interference from the face itself. Cast-shadow behavior documented — When 2D Shadow is enabled and pushback is positive, cast-shadow receiving is disabled on that material. Turning 2D Shadow off or returning pushback to 0 applies the original cast-shadow setting again. Experimental depth controls — Depth-record exclusion and receiver offset are marked as experimental. They can affect ordinary projected shadows and world post-process effects, so use them only when needed.

Follow the base map — The color resulting from the base map and texture-layer composite can be used for the outline. Follow alpha — Following the color and following the surface alpha are separate choices. Outline color and transparency can be adjusted independently.

Keep values from disabled features — Supported values from Backlight, Rim, Glitter, Outline, Reflection, Toon Specular, MatCap, and Emission are transferred more broadly while their enabled states remain distinct. Emission blending — The four Normal, Add, Screen, and Multiply blend modes and their default now match lilToon. Existing Hue, Color, and Overlay values are handled as Add. Reflection, rim, and shadow improvements — Reflection-module activation, shadow border color, Rim Shade color, Fresnel Rim range, and MatCap mask and UV handling were improved. Color-only inputs — Surface, emission, and MatCap inputs expressed only through color without a texture can also be converted. Missing and loss guidance — Materials referenced only by animation and settings without an exact counterpart are shown in the conversion report. Review the report and the rendered result after conversion.

Depth Light management — Creation, reuse, removal, and temporary build-time handling of MingToon-owned Depth Lights were reorganized. WARUDO UMod build — The build now optimizes within the exported prefab scope, connects generated shaders and textures to the bundle, and restores authored materials afterward. Prevent incomplete results — A failure to register generated assets or restore materials is reported as a build error. Depth effects depend on depth information supplied by the world, camera, and mirror. This change does not guarantee post-processing or bloom behavior in every world.

Back up the project before updating. Update through VCC for the VCC installation path, and through the MingToon update window for the DLL installation path. Materials that were already baked must be restored to editable materials and baked again for these changes to apply. Re-upload avatars already uploaded to VRChat. Reapplying a factory preset overwrites values in the selected scope. Apply only the presets you need to materials with manual adjustments. Check lighting, outlines, face proxies, and emission blending on materials that use them. If you use pushback, also check its cast-shadow receiving condition. The first bake or compile can take longer because the cache and generated-result rules changed. Later time also varies with the material and cache state. Installation and update guide · Bake and restore · 0.1.9 patch notes
Closed beta

Importing MingToon reimporting every texture in the project — the face SDF texture importer was a global AssetPostprocessor, which put every texture in the project on MingToon's dependency list. On a texture-heavy project the first import took hours. The face SDF and halftone pattern textures blocking a VRChat upload — they shipped with Streaming Mip Maps off.

Do not delete MingToon components by hand VRChat strips them on upload by itself. Deleting them manually also drops the cached renderer list, so the upload optimisation loses its scope and unoptimised materials ship as-is. → VRChat Auto face detection no longer guesses from names Auto now reads only the face flag the source material carries. Converting from Standard or URP Lit leaves every slot as Regular, so you have to mark the face slots as Face yourself. → MingToon Manager The manager's step numbers changed The order is now 1 · Convert → 2 · Setup → 3 · Advanced. Older notes will not match. caution Face Border no longer accepts negative values Below 0 the face shadow terminator sat where the head's normals barely change, and the band followed triangle edges as a staircase. Materials on the old −0.3 default now read as 0, so faces pick up slightly more shadow. Re-tune the value on your face materials. → Docs Unified Shadow now merges the cast shadow into one colour, always A projected shadow crossing into the form shadow no longer deepens where they overlap. If you want that overlap back, raise 2D Shadow Overlap Depth. → Docs

Depth Translucency — thin parts such as hair tips and hems now look like they are holding light. It measures how far light travelled through the character by reading depth twice along the light direction, so it works on its own regardless of Master Width. → Docs Upload readiness check — walks the hierarchy and the manifest and reports anything blocking an upload as a diagnostic code. → Docs Status panel — material composition, shading state, face-slot sync and optimisation scope are always visible at the top of the manager. VRChat and Quest pre-checks — counts missing standard properties and disallowed components, and reports what a Quest variant would lose. Skin role — a slot role that receives the bare-skin look values. Assign Skin Renderer Directly sets it in one go. Tab presets — save and apply presets per section, with an option to include textures. WARUDO Runtime Root — a self-contained runtime component that supplies camera depth and head direction to the shader in a Warudo mod. → Warudo Master Adjust — the first section in the inspector. An Intensity and a Tint over each of Everything That Adds Light, Every Shadow and Final Output, so a character can be retuned for a new scene in one place. Bound Added Light Too — applies the brightness ceiling after backlight, front light, fresnel rim, shadow interior reflection, 2D depth rim, depth translucency and glitter have all been added. The existing Final Lighting Maximum Multiplier runs before them, so raising a rim blew straight past it. Off by default. → Docs 2D Shadow Overlap Depth — how much the 2D shadow deepens a form shadow it lands inside, in Unified Shadow mode. Zero is a single flat colour. → Docs Paint the face area with vertex colours — mark the face region without a mask texture. It uses a different channel from the outline, so both can be painted on one mesh. Shader variant prewarm — runs automatically at the end of a conversion, and on demand from Tools > Studio Raming > MingToon > Prewarm Shader Variants.

Conversion is no longer lilToon-only — Standard, URP Lit and others convert too. In that case base colour, textures, normal, emission, occlusion and render state carry over, and everything else takes MingToon defaults. Excluded material classes — particle/VFX, refraction/gem, fur/shell, audio-reactive, flipbook/scroll, and outline-only or auxiliary passes cannot be carried over, so their originals are left untouched. → Docs Hull normal source now defaults to UV8TS — baking UV8 is the whole job; there is nothing to switch on the material afterwards. → Docs Character Root is now called MingToon Manager. lilToon Quick Convert is now called Shader Conversion. What a preset carries — values and colours only. Textures, vectors, render queue, instancing and the RenderType tag are left alone. The Face SDF Baker ships as a separate editor package. Without it installed, that button stays closed. Normal strength accepts negative values. The relief inverts. Enable Face SDF Shadow is now the master toggle at the top of the face SDF section. Everything else unfolds under it. Normal map tiling now sits directly under its slot instead of inside a fold, where it was easy to mistake for the mask's tiling outside it. The two are deliberately kept separate. Face Shading does not apply in this build. It is still in development, so the section is hidden and any material or preset carrying it enabled is read back as off. Face conversion and every other face feature work as normal.

UV channel occupancy — shows whether UV4 · UV7 · UV8 are free or in use, and warns that UV7 is shared between the face normal bake and the face SDF projection, so only one can own it. Conversion pair audit — verifies converted materials against their sources. It is slow, so it runs only when you press the button. Face module sync — warns when a face slot's keyword disagrees with its material value and fixes them in one action. Baking in that state drops face shading. Optimisation scope warning — tells you how many renderers would upload unoptimised when the cache is stale. Editor runtime preview — preview look profiles and runtime face direction in the editor. None of it ships to a VRChat upload. The material cost estimate moved next to the search box. One line, expandable for the breakdown. Vertex painting — live overlay, X-axis symmetry, brush strength and opacity, and a movable window. It no longer stalls on every stroke. Conversion tab — directly assigned renderers now show up in the slot summary, and skin is counted separately from face and regular. You can choose whether shadow colour and fresnel are overwritten, and re-apply a look preset to an already converted character. Per-section and look preset lists are laid out by category instead of hidden behind a dropdown.

A second line drawn beside the face form shadow's edge — the border was built on the body terminator rather than the face one. Projected shadows falling on slots marked as face. Cast and 2D shadows not converging to one colour in Unified Shadow — the outline hull and the additional-light path never reached the brightness ceiling, so only those kept burning. The master not reaching the fallback rim, the second of the two depth rims, which changed the result on cameras with no depth buffer. The Scene view freezing for minutes — the post-processing bridge was rescanning every loaded object on each Scene view event. Baked textures blocking a VRChat upload — the mask pack, surface flatten, and face SDF outputs were written with Streaming Mip Maps off.

The documentation site is now available in 한국어 · English · 日本語. Switch at the top right. New Internals section — shader pass structure, the performance cost formula, what the bake removes, how to read a conversion report, and the VRChat compatibility rules. → Docs The control reference is generated from the MingToon source, so it always matches what the inspector displays. Added full-text search.
Closed Beta · 2026-08-05

Check your VRChat Expression Parameters budget first Non-Destructive Modular Avatar Install is enabled by default and uses 21 synced parameters · 154 bits for Virtual Light and Master Adjust. Installation stops if the total exceeds 256 bits when combined with the existing avatar. → VRChat Face Shading hidden in 0.1.3 is back Face Shading is visible and usable again. After updating, check the masks, boundaries, and SDF map on existing face materials, then enable it manually. → Character Expression

Hybrid PBR — Adds metallic, smoothness, direct highlights, and environment reflections while retaining toon diffuse lighting, then shapes reflections with toon blending. → Docs Toon Specular — Adds Isotropic or hair-specific Anisotropic highlights without enabling full PBR. → Docs Region Mask — Divides one RGBA texture into four regions to adjust metallic, smoothness, reflection, and Toon Specular per part. → Docs Face SDF Studio included — Previews Base, Nose, Cheek, Lip, and Eye Socket in real time and bakes them into one directional SDF. → Docs Single-channel face SDF — Adds the Single Channel (Grayscale) format, which mirrors one R channel for both sides. → Docs SceneView vertex and mask painting — Provides Paint, Harden, Smooth, Hard Face, X symmetry, connected islands, mesh isolation, and explicit save/discard flow. → Docs MaskMaker included with the MM button — Opens Selection, Gradient, Bridge Random, and Brush Paint directly from actual mask slots and applies PNGs to slots. Virtual Light and Master Adjust VRC menu — Adjusts the color, brightness, and intensity of Virtual Light, Highlight, Shadow, and Final Output from the VRC menu, with Reset All restoring defaults. → Docs MingToon 2D Projection Shadow Caster — Excludes glasses and accessories from MingToon's depth-based effect while preserving regular rendering and Unity real-time shadows. → Docs

Face SDF Studio and MaskMaker are included in one 0.1.4 package; both are Editor-only and add no runtime scripts. The Face SDF Studio workspace is organized into two steps — follow only Preparation · Front UV7 and SDF Creation · Preview · Bake. The outline width mask was moved closer to the width settings, and its Tiling/Offset are now preserved during lilToon conversion. Inspector categories and descriptions now use the user-facing names, with tooltips placed where needed instead of a separate guide tab.

Reduced repeated calculations in the Inspector, presets, and material cost panel to cut unnecessary updates when editing multiple materials. Reused Renderer/feature analysis and Mask Pack readback in the Bake path to avoid reading the same data repeatedly. Improved Bake cancellation and restore safety, clarifying boundaries for cancellation during preparation, final save, and restoration of meshes, blend shapes, and original materials. Changed VRC menu installation to a non-destructive workflow, preserving existing Root Menu, Expression Parameters, and FX and merging only in the build clone.

Base Pass disappeared when enabling Face Shading — restored BRP ForwardBase and URP UniversalForwardOnly, and replaced the development full-fixed compilation that exceeded D3D11 resource limits with a safe default. White zigzag lines appeared on backlit faces — capped the screen-derivative width of shape-shadow boundaries so triangle edges no longer show through shading. Face SDF direction/coordinates were misaligned or transitions jumped abruptly; added an unassigned-map warning and recovery path. lilToon outline width masks and Tiling/Offset were not converted. EndLayoutGroup errors occurred after Manager conversion, saving, or refreshing. Emission disappeared because color and intensity were multiplied to black when no emission map was assigned.
Rewrote the face SDF and Face SDF Studio, Face Shading, Hybrid PBR/Toon Specular/Region Mask, and VRChat Virtual Light installation documentation for 0.1.4.
Closed Beta · 2026-08-07

caution A new material's Base HSVG hue now defaults to 0 instead of 0.02 Materials made up to 0.1.4 keep their saved 0.02. If an untouched base map looked rotated by about seven degrees, set the hue back to 0 or use the property's right-click reset. The factory look presets have been replaced SoftCartoon is gone; Soft Toon, Hard Toon, and Rim Shadow take its place, each with a - Low lightweight variant. Materials you already applied a preset to keep their values — only the list you can pick from changes. The lilToon conversion mesh addressing rule changed The first conversion after updating rebakes the meshes once. From then on, pulling the same avatar into the scene again reuses what is already baked. → Docs

SSAO (Screen Space Occlusion) — Re-reads the camera depth per pixel to darken necks, armpits, cloth folds, and where feet meet the floor. It is not a light and not a post-process pass, so it disappears silently wherever no depth exists. → Docs Shadow Color Map — Distributes the single unified-shadow colour through a UV map so hair and skin can hold different shadow colours. White is the neutral value, so turning it on alone changes nothing. → Docs Screen added to the screentone's Pattern Space — Locks the lattice to the viewport and lets the character slide underneath: the overprinted screentone or pop-art reading. It cannot bend or shimmer when the field of view or the camera angle changes. → Docs Glitter Enable Shape Map — Replaces each particle's silhouette with a texture. Six shapes ship in Textures/Glitter/: Star, Bloom, Sparkle, Heart, Hex, and Flower. → Docs Glitter Rotation Randomize — Turns each particle to a different angle. Lower it to 0 to stand a directional shape such as a heart upright. Glitter Use Color Too — Reads one mask as full RGBA: alpha is the region and RGB tints the particles. It costs no extra texture read. Fresnel Rim View Strength — Chooses whether the view or the light decides where the rim sits. At 0 the rim stays put as the camera turns. → Docs Create a look preset from a prefab — Right-click a prefab in the Project window → Studio Raming / MingToon / Create Look Preset From Prefab. It pulls a Common · Face · Skin set out of a character you already finished shading. VRChat Preview — Tools / Studio Raming / MingToon / VRChat Preview switches the editor view to what an upload actually shows, with camera depth either absent or available. A scene-view banner stays up while it is on. → Docs

Shadow Pattern (Screentone) is now its own tab. No longer a group inside Shadow Color, it has its own master toggle, preset row, and copy/paste. → Docs The screentone can be switched from in-game. The authoring shader no longer compiles the module out, so Enable Shadow Pattern can be driven by an ordinary float animation or a VRChat expression menu. Rim / Added Light Maximum Multiplier now defaults to 3 instead of 2. The factory look presets were aligned to the same value; the rest of the Lighting Brightness Limits group is unchanged. → Docs Renamed to Cast MingToon 2D Projected Shadow — the ...Caster of 0.1.4. Behaviour is the same. A look preset may make a material cheaper but never quietly dearer. - Low presets still switch heavy modules off; only the direction that raises cost is blocked.

Less blue waiting when toggling a module. The eight look modules that get toggled most (matcap, Fresnel rim, toon specular, backlight, front light, rim shade, emission, occlusion) are now compiled into the authoring shader up front, so toggling them recompiles nothing. The cost of a baked result is unchanged. Lighting variants are compiled once, right after install. Directional, point, spot, and vertex-light combinations you actually create while working are warmed ahead of time, so switching a light off or dropping a new one in no longer stalls. Run it again from Tools / Studio Raming / MingToon / Warm up shader variants. lilToon conversion reuses meshes it already baked. A single (1) suffix Unity appends to a copy gave the same avatar a new address every time, so everything was rebaked. → Docs The depth mask is read once per fragment. SSAO and the 2D shadow were reading the same texture at the same UV twice. The Shadow Interior Reflection mask now has a keyword of its own, dropping instructions and one texture sample on materials that do not use it. → Docs

A material with Cast MingToon 2D Projected Shadow off turned dark all over — the transparent depth prepass was gated on the same switch, and the disabled material's depth modules read what stood behind its own body, painting a rim and an inner edge across a whole pair of glasses. → Docs Raising the screentone's Pattern Edge Softness printed marks on lit surfaces holding no shadow — the blur is now bounded by the mark. At softness 0 the result is identical to before. → Docs The screentone's Overlay was indistinguishable from Recolor — the ink reached past the shadow. It is now confined to the shadow. Toon specular went black on the Screen and Overlay blend modes — an [HDR] colour or an intensity above 1 flipped the formula negative. Hue and Color had the same defect and were fixed with it. → Docs The face assist offsets ran even on materials with the 2D shadow switched off — a material that inherited only the value from a preset lost its projected shadow on the face and received nothing in return. → Docs Inspector guidance corrections — the Cast MingToon 2D Projected Shadow tooltip described the opposite of what the switch does, and turning unified shadow off can change the look in one step because each layer's stored colour returns, which is now warned about. Depth modules also say so when the material is absent from camera depth.

The manual gained Lighting Brightness Limits and Unified Shadow sections in all three languages. Unified shadow is on by default and hides the per-layer shadow colours on a new material, and nothing said why. Three SSAO descriptions were corrected against the code: it is not multiplied with the occlusion map but joins after the toon band and the screentone taking whichever is darker, it scatters no per-pixel noise, and the far-distance fade begins at 75% of that value. The VRChat compatibility document's account of the face coordinate frame was corrected to the path that actually ships. → Docs
Closed Beta · 2026-08-18

Run the schema migration once Tools > Studio Raming > MingToon > Advanced > Migrate Project To Current Schema The material schema moved from 10 to 11. The new Enable Fresnel Rim Mask and Enable Rim Shade Mask toggles read as off on older materials, so until you run this, those materials apply no rim mask at all. The migration finds masks that are not the plain white default and switches the toggles on. → Installation Bake caches regenerate, and VRChat avatars must be re-uploaded The generated shader cache version moved from 28 to 29, which invalidates existing bake output. The next build rebakes it automatically — nothing to clean up by hand, but that one build takes longer. Shaders are bundled in the avatar asset bundle, so an avatar already uploaded keeps the old shader until you upload it again. caution Force On in Depth Availability now excludes mirrors Force On now means "enable even where the host cannot report it, except in mirrors". Inside a mirror the depth modules stand down whatever you picked. → Docs Missing Depth Fallback (the Fresnel fallback) has been removed Depth Rim no longer falls back to a Fresnel rim when depth is missing. A material that had the fallback mode set to Fresnel loses that rim. Depth modules now simply stand down when there is no depth. caution Include Shading on the outline behaves differently The outline is now drawn from the base map colour and the lighting response alone; it no longer redraws the body's shadow pattern, cast shadows, or depth effects on top of the line. Include Shading now applies a light shading band that follows the form shadow colour instead of duplicating the whole body shading. → Docs caution Compile All Modules While Authoring now defaults to on This is what keeps a toggle from waiting on a shader recompile while you work. The console prints one line the first time it turns on, and you can switch it off in the bulk edit panel. Unnecessary keywords are still stripped on build, so leaving it on costs the shipped avatar nothing.

Color Adjust Mask — limits the Base HSVG adjustment to where the mask is white, so you can recolour the eyes and leave the face alone. lilToon's colour adjust mask lands here on conversion. → Docs Mask Texture Color added to Toon Specular Color Source — the RGB painted into the mask becomes the highlight colour, so hair highlights can differ strand by strand. No extra texture read. → Docs Shadow Mode selector — one row decides whether bangs and props cast real shadows on the face or are drawn as a soft 2D shadow. Values that used to be split across two tabs are now set together. → Docs Compute For Edited-Normal Models on the outline UV8 bake — re-derives the outline direction from the mesh's own faces, for hair and skirts whose normals came off a sphere or a cylinder. Off by default, so an already baked character keeps the line it has. → Docs Carry Depth Light on Upload (off by default) — adds one light to the VRChat upload only, so the camera draws depth. Everyone who sees you pays for it, which is why the inspector states the four costs before the box can matter. → Docs Enable Fresnel Rim Mask · Enable Rim Shade Mask — the two rim masks now work like the shadow reflection mask: a material that does not use one never samples the texture. Turn the toggle on before you assign a mask. → Docs Diagnostic added to Depth Availability — paints the avatar a flat colour that says which depth texture the shader was actually reading. For bug reports only. → Docs VRC Light Volumes (off by default) — in a world that uses VRC Light Volumes, the character's indirect light lift and shadow tint follow the room's volume instead of Unity's probes. Built-in only, and it falls back to probes where there are no volumes. Heal Material Keywords (Project) menu — brings every MingToon material's stored keywords and pass state back in line with its inspector values. It confirms first, backs up what it changes, and logs one line. The Manager says up front when the outline UV8 bake is needed — if Normal Source is UV8TS and the mesh has no UV8, a warning and a bake button appear at the top of the MingToon Manager. The button states where the new meshes go and how many renderers it will process. → Docs Use Shadow Color Map and Color Map Amount added to the bulk edit panel — set them across a multi-material selection in one pass. → Docs

Missing Depth Fallback (the Fresnel fallback) has been removed. Depth modules stand down when there is no depth. The outline (classic hull) costs about a third of what it did per pixel. It no longer duplicates the body's shading. → Docs Force On in Depth Availability now excludes mirrors. → Docs Compile All Modules While Authoring now defaults to on. The Prewarm Shader Variants menu is gone. Warm up shader variants does the same job and stays.

Inspector toggles no longer wait on a shader compile. The 2–6 second recompile is gone from Enable Glitter Mask, Use Mask (shadow reflection), 2D Shadow Mask, Depth Rim Mask, Inner Edge Mask, Enable Region Mask, Enable 2nd Shadow, the layer dropdowns, Base Tint After HSVG, and Face Shading Module. The picture it draws and the defaults are unchanged. Shader compilation finishes once, at package import. It runs in parallel behind a cancellable progress bar, and afterwards there is no compile wait during conversion, material selection, or editing. A cancelled run is picked up where it stopped. Conversion reports its progress by stage. A progress bar walks material conversion → look preset → mesh bakes, and the per-stage timings land in the console on completion. → Docs Layer masks are composited into one packed texture automatically. Surface stack, normal and MatCap masks are combined so the GPU reads fewer textures. How you use them and every adjustment stays the same; the composites are generated and shared under MingToonGenerated/MaskPacks. The outline panel reports whether the mesh has UV8 and vertex colours. → Docs The outline UV8 bake no longer rejects an already baked character. It skips UV8 that MingToon baked, rejects only the user model's own UV8, and names the mesh. Inspector text fixes — toolbar and section header labels no longer clip, the sticky header no longer flickers while you resize the inspector, and help and warning boxes are set at body size.

Upload optimisation (baking) was forcing disabled modules back on — the root cause behind avatars glowing white in mirrors and in cameras without post. Turning Enable Emission off no longer produces full-screen emission from the default white map, and a disabled 2D Shadow Mask stays disabled. 2D Shadow and Depth Rim slipped instead of following the body inside a VRChat mirror — the shader was reading the player camera's depth buffer, so it wore a stranger's silhouette. Depth modules now stand down inside mirrors. → Docs Shading collapsed into pale flatness in worlds without a realtime directional light and in Disable Pixel Lights mirrors — the ambient probe now synthesises a key light so shading holds everywhere. Worlds with a directional light are unchanged. → Docs lilToon conversion carried the values but left the modules off — Enable PBR Surface, Enable Emission, Enable Surface Stack, Outline Master and Enable Classic Hull now come out on. Stack layers 2 and 3 arrive, and outline direction and thickness are correct. → Docs Outlines shifted diagonally with Normal Source set to VertexColorTS on a mesh with no vertex colours — it now falls back to mesh normals. → Docs One part with no tangents or normals killed the outline, face, and height bakes together — only that renderer is skipped now, and the console names the mesh. Baking made one copy per renderer when several renderers shared a mesh — one asset per source mesh now, shared by all of them. Conversion erased the user model's UV8 regardless of Overwrite Occupied UV Channels — with the option off it skips and reports. Unified Shadow Color Map would not switch off while the global compile mode was on — it now switches off reliably in any compile mode. → Docs Dropping MingToon or a converted avatar into a VRChat world project broke it with a VRCExpressionsMenu compile error (CS0246) — the expression menu installer compiles away in world projects. Selecting or editing a material in a Unity 2022 project made the base vanish and left only the outline — the root cause is fixed, including on setups where waiting for the compile never helped. → Troubleshooting The first conversion applied the top look preset instead of the one you picked — the selection now survives a script reload and a reselect. → Docs Look presets switched off the MatCap, normal layers and surface stack that conversion had brought across, and forced every blend mode to Add — look presets now handle the look only and leave layer content alone. The [MingToon] VRChat build hook compiled and registered. confirmation never appeared — it now prints once per editor session. → VRChat Materials that never used the toon specular mask were sampling it anyway — split behind a use toggle, along with the two rim masks.

The question-mark buttons in the inspector and the MingToon Manager now open the matching section of this site. The property reference was regenerated from the current source. The deleted Fallback Display section is gone, and new rows — Depth Availability, Toon Specular Color Source, Face Shading Module and others — are in all three languages.

Open beta · 2026-09-07 0.1.7 is the cumulative open-beta release after 0.1.6. Check before upgrading ⚠️ Coming from 0.1.6 or earlier, delete the whole Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon folder and import 0.1.7 fresh. That is the official upgrade path. Importing over the old folder can leave scripts, shaders and generated files that no longer exist in 0.1.7, causing duplicate assemblies or compile errors. So many property names changed in this release that a value stored on a 0.1.6 material does not carry over — a name that is gone leaves the shader default in its place, the material keeps working without an error, and you dial it back in from the new defaults with no conversion or migration step. A saved Look Preset gets you back there quickly. Bake output — generated shaders, flattened textures and mask packs — has to be baked again as well. If you created presets or other user files directly under Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon, back them up outside that folder first; then delete only the old MingToon folder and import the new package. Materials, textures and prefabs stored elsewhere in the project are not part of this deletion. The separately distributed MingLightController folder is not part of it either. ⚠️ The _Ming prefix was dropped from material property IDs. Animation curves must be re-bound. Most property IDs that began with _Ming through 0.1.6 are now the unprefixed canonical name (_MingBacklightColor → _BacklightColor, _MingGlitterDensity → _GlitterDensity, _MingAllEffectsEnabled → _AllEffectsEnabled, about 670 in all). There is no automatic conversion. A value stored on a 0.1.6 material, and any animation curve pointing at material._Ming..., now names something the shader does not declare, so the value silently falls back to the shader default. Dial the materials back in from the new defaults as described above, and re-bind the animation curves to the new IDs. Presets and JSON documents written against the old IDs can simply be saved again from a current material. If you want a list of the materials, presets and animation clips still using an old ID, StudioRaming/MingToon/Advanced/Migrate Project To Current Schema validates and reports — it is not required for the upgrade, and it does not rewrite curves. Some _Ming names stay (_MingVirtualLight*, _MingMaterialVersion, _MingUnifiedShadow* and others), so do not strip the prefix everywhere. ⚠️ Bake caches regenerate, and VRChat avatars must be re-uploaded. The generated shader cache version moved up, which invalidates existing bake output. The next build rebakes it automatically — nothing to clean up by hand, but that one build takes longer. This release's MatCap optimisation only applies once you rebake. Shaders are bundled in the avatar asset bundle, so an avatar already uploaded must be uploaded again to receive this fix. ⚠️ Face shading and shadow shape change on some materials. In both cases the old behaviour was the bug. Shading that popped hard as the light crossed the centre of the face now moves across smoothly, and the face depth offset that was wrongly applied to the whole body on a unified material with the face region vertex-painted is gone. ⚠️ Lighting defaults changed. Nine lighting defaults, including Scene Light Color Influence and Indirect Light Lift, were retuned to match a real production setup, and Enable Translucency now defaults to off. This applies only to newly created materials and the factory presets; materials you already made are left untouched. 2D Rim Light gained Scene Light Influence. It defaults to 1, so existing materials without a saved value may also show a darker rim inside a dark light volume. Set Scene Light Influence in 2D Rim Light to 0 to disable this influence. ⚠️ Additional Light Energy Cap is new. Point and spot lights are held back more than they used to be. It caps the energy that additional lights such as point and spot add to the final surface brightness, and the shader default is 0.35 — the value at which a highlight under a strong coloured light keeps its colour instead of blowing out to white. It limits the brightness contribution only, so the additional light's colour still comes through as before. A value stored on a 0.1.6 material does not carry over, so on a project you deleted the folder from and imported fresh every material starts at that 0.35 default. If additional lights feel darker than before, raise Additional Light Energy Cap under Lighting. ⚠️ 2D Shadow Bias changed scale by 10x in this release. 1 now means 10 cm, not 1 cm. A value stored on a 0.1.6 material does not carry over, so there is nothing to convert by hand - dial the value in again on the new scale. The bundled Soft Toon presets are stored on the new scale. The same pass removed the Depth Blur and Light Pushback rows: Receiver Depth Pushback now affects camera depth only. ⚠️ Face SDF Studio and Mask Maker are no longer bundled from this release on. Both tools are now separate products. Buy either one and drop it into the project, and the matching place in the inspector integrates with it exactly as before. Without it, that button becomes a notice — nothing else is affected. ⚠️ VRChat Expressions menu authoring was split out of the MingToon core package. The old installer UI was removed from the Manager. The separately sold Ming Light Controller (MLC) add-on now owns per-avatar menu, parameter and FX authoring. Without MLC, only the generated runtime menu is unavailable; the MingToon shader and the Build Depth Light choice still work normally. Menus, parameters and FX layers physically installed by an earlier release are not removed automatically, so clean them up by hand if you no longer want them. ⚠️ The URP backend ships as a separate add-on. The base package contains BRP and the shared core only. The URP shader and its Renderer Features are delivered separately as MingToon_URP_Addon_0.1.7.unitypackage, included in the paid distribution download. If you have been using MingToon in a URP project, import the base package first and the add-on after it. Installing the add-on on its own is not a supported configuration. In a project without the add-on the URP shader does not appear among the shader choices, while the shared editor features still compile and work. VRChat PC and Quest do not use URP, so neither is affected by the split (PC uses the BRP baked version, Quest the mobile conversion). The add-on targets WARUDO and general Unity projects on URP 12.x. The bundled MingToon_URP_Addon.md documents the install order and everything included.

The cleanup module included only in this version runs by itself, once per project, the first time the 0.1.7 editor code loads. It runs the same whether you imported over the old package or deleted the folder and imported fresh - 0.1.6 generated output lives in Assets/StudioRaming/MingToonGenerated/Shaders, not inside Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon, so deleting the MingToon folder leaves it behind. The module picks only the obsolete 0.1.6-style fixed profiles it can prove MingToon generated, redirects the baked materials using that exact profile to the current canonical BRP/URP shader, and then deletes the profile. That is what prevents a Missing Shader. It does not change any material values beyond the shader reference, original/editable materials, or foreign shaders/assets in other folders. If the current BRP/URP shader it would redirect to is unavailable or has errors, it keeps the profile and reports that in the Console. Old parameters are not translated to the new layout, so the look may change. To obtain the correct current-version look, convert the original/editable materials again and then Bake. By default, MingToon Manager saves editable materials and generated Mesh assets together in a MingToon folder beside the original Model/FBX. If you specify a conversion output folder, both use that folder. MingToon-owned Mesh assets previously stored in the global MingToonGenerated/Meshes folder are moved beside their original source during the next conversion, while preserving their GUID, .meta, and Renderer references. When a Model/FBX with the same GUID is overwritten, reimported, or moved, its registered generated Mesh assets are automatically rebaked after import completes. Mesh assets that can be safely reused are updated in place, preserving their GUIDs and Renderer references. MingToon does not overwrite assets automatically when the Renderer scope has changed, the source Mesh cannot be identified unambiguously, or the user has made conflicting edits to the generated Mesh's geometry, colors, or UVs. Check the warning and convert again in MingToon Manager. New features
documents.s: Cleanup of 0.1.6 Generated Assets and Automatic Updating of Converted Meshes

documents.t: A second emission map, so different areas can glow in different colours. The two layers are added, so each area keeps its own colour. Off by default.
Uses the emission map's alpha channel as a per-pixel intensity mask. The alpha is already read along with the colour, so it costs no extra texture read. Present on both emission layers.

Copy and paste buttons were added to the inspector's top bar. Paste comes in five variants — Paste All, Paste Values Only (No Textures), Paste Textures Only, Paste Keywords Only and Paste Render Queue Only — so you can carry settings across while leaving each material's own textures in place. Undo (Ctrl+Z) works.

The controls that take effect across the whole material are gathered in one place at the top of the inspector, Unified Shadow Color among them. Gamma was added to Unified Shadow and SSAO tone controls, Normal Outline Color, and Inner Outline Color. It adjusts only the value axis, preserving hue and saturation; 1 preserves the existing look. Outline opacity and width are unchanged.
documents.s: 4. Quick Settings card and color Gamma

documents.t: The SSAO tab in the Depth group settles into the form this release ships. Coming straight from 0.1.6 the tab itself is new to you. It reads screen depth to find where objects meet and darkens only those places; unlike an occlusion map it is applied after the toon bands and the screentone, so it never stair-steps a shadow edge. It is off by default, so no existing material changes. The units and ranges moved since the module was first described. SSAO Radius is 0.001-0.03 (default 0.005), and what was described as a fade range is now called Contact Falloff: a multiple of SSAO Radius rather than metres (0.25-4, default 1). SSAO Bias is likewise a ratio of SSAO Radius rather than absolute metres (0.4 = 40% of the radius). Being a ratio of the radius, the look follows along when the camera distance or the radius changes. The far distance is no longer an SSAO-only row: it merged into Shared Fade Distance (default 200), which the 2D shadow uses as well. Do not carry figures over from an older release. Like every other depth module it needs the camera depth texture. It disappears silently where depth is unavailable, switches off with All Effects and with the Depth Effects Master, and is off on the VRC Low quality tier. The Build Depth Light also counts an SSAO-enabled avatar as a depth-module user. The cost is paid per visible fragment, not once per material. The depth group's Shared Quality sets the depth samples per pixel (Low 4, Standard 8, High 16), and Shared Fade Distance is the control that ends the cost — a character past that distance takes zero samples, which makes lowering it the surest optimisation in a crowded scene. Both rows are shared with the 2D shadow, so neither can be adjusted for one module alone. Visibility in Cast Shadow and Visibility in 2D Shadow set how much of the occlusion is still drawn inside each shadow. Manual section 3-10. SSAO documents every control.

The 2D shadow is now one silhouette sheet. The front object's silhouette is shifted away from the light and that one sheet is read, then pushed farther the more the front object floats off the receiver - what rests on the surface stays at the width and only what floats moves out, which is what reads as depth. The shadow is judged against the receiver's own tangent plane, so the marks the face's and body's own curvature used to leave are gone while the shadow of bangs almost touching the forehead survives. The 2D Shadow tab settles on these controls: Shadow Width, Shadow Intensity, Depth Stretch, Depth Curve, Depth Falloff, Softness, Blur, 2D Shadow Bias, Receiver Depth Pushback and Suppress Backlit Silhouette. Depth Stretch (default 1) is what creates the depth. At 1 an object floating 10 cm away lands its shadow 10 cm past the width; at 0 nothing is pushed and the sheet is read at the width only. Depth Curve sets the shape of that push and Depth Falloff how strong a far-floating object's shadow stays. The further the camera looks down at the character, the shorter Depth Stretch eases and the thinner the stretched part gets. The push is a screen direction, so looking down used to leave the shadow reading as a long smear; a side-lit shadow pushed across the screen is untouched. There is no control for it; it is automatic. That shortening now reaches materials using Face Fixed Direction as well. The face was exempt until now, on the grounds that it pins its shadow direction to the head, so with the camera looking down at it only the bangs shadow kept its full length while the body's shadow at the same angle shortened correctly. What is pinned is the direction the shadow points, not its length, so the direction still follows the head and only the length now shortens with the camera angle. The stretched part and the part at the width shorten together, so how a side-facing surface fades out is exactly what it was. The length never collapses to nothing. A floor keeps the shadow axis defined, and at that floor the shadow is 2% of the Shadow Width you set - a size no one sees. Blur is applied last, to the finished shadow, and its radius comes from that value in metres alone. Only then is the sheet read five times - the centre read plus a four-tap rotating disc. The inside of the shadow is painted solid in the shadow colour you chose. On a material using the unified shadow a fully covered area comes out exactly the colour of the form shadow's core, and the Shadow Boundary band lands only on an edge softened by Blur or by depth. The quality and distance rows merged into two shared controls in the depth group, Shared Quality and Shared Fade Distance. Shared Quality sets SSAO's sample count only; the 2D shadow ignores the tier and reads a fixed handful - one at the width, four votes, one sheet read, and with Blur on that sheet read becomes five, ten at most. SSAO now exposes Color Purity (0-10, default 1), Color Brightness and Color Gamma; default purity 1 preserves the composed color. The old SSAO Saturation name is not a shader property. Manual section 3-11. 2D Shadow: one silhouette sheet and its depth response documents each control.
documents.s: 2D Shadow: one silhouette sheet and its depth response

documents.t: You can now choose how the backlight and the front light mix their color into the surface: Normal, Multiply, Add, Hue, Screen, Color or Overlay - the same list the other rim modules use. The Blend Opacity (0-1) added beside it lowers the effect's presence without touching its color or intensity. Both default to Add at opacity 1. That combination is the same expression as the previous direct addition, so this entry alone changes nothing. Outside Add, Backlight Intensity and Front Light Intensity act as how much is mixed in rather than a brightness multiplier. Hue and Color cannot hold a hue above a luminance of 1 and drift to gray there, so use Add or Screen when you want the layer to burn.
documents.s: Backlight Blend Mode and Front Light Blend Mode

documents.t: A button was added at the bottom of Setup > 1 · Convert > Mesh Channels To Bake in the Manager. Press it after editing the source FBX and it rebakes only the channels ticked above - outline normals, face normals, character height. Materials and look values are not touched. Running the conversion again to get the meshes back would rewrite both, and re-applying a look preset over hand-tuned values is exactly what this button avoids. The scope selector above the group picks Every mesh on this character or Selected objects only. It is disabled when there is no target mesh, no channel ticked, or the output folder is not valid.

The lilToon 2.3.4 material path was remapped for HSVG, alpha masks, outline width and vertex pressure, rim direction and backface conditions, MatCap mask channels, reflection color, and toon specular. The report now warns only for values that cannot be represented; equivalent defaults and empty no-op masks are not counted as failures. Main Color, 2nd and 3rd layers and their independent masks are imported. The 2nd and 3rd layers become MingToon stacking layers so their color, mask and blend conditions remain independent. The base surface, alpha mask, ten stacking layers, emission layers 1 and 2, and their masks share one UV router. UV0-UV3, Tiling/Offset, scrolling, rotation around the center, rotation speed, and sprite-sheet columns, rows, frame count and playback speed use the same implementation. lilToon decal position, size and rotation; single-image versus tiled display; left/right restriction; copy, flip and mirror modes; and sprite-sheet animation are converted. Atlas textures that move like an animated image are supported; this release does not include a video-file decoder. UV routing is compiled only into a generated shader that uses it. A material that uses the default UV and static textures does not pay the extra routing or atlas work. Automatic rewriting of old material-property curves inside AnimationClips, and Fur, Gem and refraction conversion, are outside this release.
documents.s: lilToon 2.3.4 conversion fidelity and the shared UV router

documents.t: Conversion results are grouped as source-and-result pairs instead of one long paragraph per material. Each pair prints both material paths under Source: and Converted:, states how the two were matched under Resolution:, and then splits what could not be carried across into two lists, Core mismatches and Explicit losses. Expand the Last Conversion Result panel for that detail, and Copy All takes the whole report in one action. Resolution is one of Matched by provenance, Matched by unique name, Ambiguous name; review required and Source missing. The first two mean the pair is settled; the last two mean you have to check which original the material came from yourself. UV, decal, emission, alpha and outline settings that are immediately visible on clothing are converted as far as the destination can represent them instead of being left as warnings. Only features without a rendering path in this release, such as Fur, Gem and refraction, remain as Explicit losses. A warning now sits under Direct Face Renderer and Direct Skin Renderer. It counts the MingToon materials on those named renderers that are not marked with that role yet - so many face, so many skin - and points at the Mark Roles on the Named Renderers button right below it. Without the role mark a look preset cannot route its face and skin values to those materials and they end up painted with the regular ones, and until now nothing on screen said so. It counts exactly what the button marks, so when the warning goes the marking is done. It appears in all three languages.

The VRChat lighting and look-control menu generator was separated from the MingToon core package into a separately sold add-on named Ming Light Controller (MLC). MingToon updates and avatar-menu authoring can now be managed independently, and users who do not need a runtime menu do not need to install the add-on. A Ming Light Controller Settings component now stores the expression profile, the attachment mode and the per-feature adjustments on the avatar root. Those values used to live in the window alone, so the last avatar you touched decided the next one's setup and nothing survived a script recompile. Two characters in one project can now carry different menus and parameter budgets. Add it by right-clicking a prefab in the Project window and choosing MingToon > Ming Light Controller, or from the button in the Attachment window. Only the entries you actually changed are recorded, so returning one to the catalog default removes its record. It holds authoring intent only and does nothing at run time.
documents.s: Per-avatar Ming Light Controller settings (separately sold add-on)

documents.t: Two rows joined the bottom of the Master Adjust tab: Performance Distance (m) (default 10) and Performance Distance Scale (default 1). The camera distance is split into near, mid and far bands against the product of the two, and whole modules are cut as the camera moves away. Within 0.4x of that product (4 m by default) nothing changes at all. Past it (4-10 m by default) the four camera-depth modules, PBR, matcap layers 2 and up, normal layers 2 and up, stack layers 3 and up, glitter, screen tone and the shadow interior reflection switch off, and the sample-count tiers step down once. Beyond 10 m what remains is base colour, the first form shadow, the cast shadow, outlines, emission, rim shade and the face SDF. It is combined with the existing VRC Quality Tier by taking the lower of the two. Mid caps where quality tier Mid does and far where Low does, so a material already set to Low stays Low however close the camera gets. The band is decided per object - the renderer's origin against the camera - so every pixel of a character takes the same one. It switches at the threshold; the gradual disappearance is still Shared Fade Distance's job. The scale is what the separately sold MLC add-on drives from an in-game radial: turn it down to 0 in a crowded instance to pin the avatar to its cheapest state, raise it for photos to keep the near look further out. Neither row folds into a baked constant, so both keep working after upload. The defaults change no look. What you see up close is unchanged; only distant avatars get cheaper.
documents.s: Performance Distance — the heavy modules switch off outright with distance

documents.t: The four Surface Mode options were renamed to carry their render queue: Opaque (2000), Cutout (2450), Semi-Transparent (2499) and Transparent (3000). 0.1.6's Transparent · Outline Depth Ready is Semi-Transparent (2499). Only the names changed — each mode's render state, queue and stored value are as they were — so no existing material looks different. The difference between the two transparent modes is now spelled out in the option's own description. Semi-Transparent (2499) uses alpha blending and writes depth as well. At render queue 2499 it lands in the camera depth texture, so it is the mode to be on if you want 2D Shadow, 2D Rim Light or Inner Outline on a transparent surface. Because it has depth, it suits a surface where the far side must not cover the near one, such as double-sided hair. Transparent (3000) is standard alpha blending. It writes no depth and draws back to front, so overlapping layers sharing one material — body, underwear and skirt — show through each other instead of erasing one another. It is also the side for a surface that has to blend with other transparent objects, glass among them. In exchange it stays out of the camera depth texture, so the three modules above are unavailable. Both modes can keep their outlines.
documents.s: Surface Mode option names tidied up

documents.t: Two-Sided Dual Pass was added to Surface Rendering. It draws the far side of a surface whose Visible Faces is Off (Double-Sided) in its own pass, before the near side. The per-triangle sawtooth where a skirt flap folds across itself disappears, and the far side blends through by alpha. The cost is one vertex pass and one SetPass. Pixel cost is unchanged — a double-sided surface was already shading both facings. It can be switched on independently of Surface Mode. It is off by default, so no existing material looks different.

A Transparent (3000) material writes no depth while it draws colour, so its outline showed through the surface toward the camera. Turning on Transparent Depth Prepass under Surface Rendering draws one more depth-only pass and rejects that outline. Semi-Transparent (2499) writes depth itself and does not need it, so the option only takes effect on Transparent (3000). If a back-side outline still shows through a fold seen edge-on, raise Outline Reject Margin (Slope) and Outline Reject Margin (Constant) a little at a time. Both default to 0, and overdoing it erases the silhouette outline along with it.
documents.s: Transparent Depth Prepass — an outline no longer shows through a transparent material

documents.t: An Alpha Fades area was added to Alpha & Cutout. Enable Distance Fade fades the surface out by how far it is from the camera. Use it to keep your own head or accessories out of your own view in first person, or to make something disappear as it gets further away. The near side is set by Near - Fully Gone At and Near - Fully Visible At, the far side by Far - Starts Fading At and Far - Fully Gone At (in metres); equal values in a pair give a hard switch at that distance. Enable Fresnel Alpha varies transparency with how squarely the surface faces the camera. Opacity Facing Camera and Opacity At Silhouette decide the direction between them, which is why there is no mode to pick. It reads the mesh's own facing rather than a normal map, so it follows the silhouette. Both are off by default, and the ranges you get the moment you switch one on hide nothing, so set the distances and the opacities yourself. An Opaque (2000) Surface Mode hides the result. Two caveats. Transparent Depth Prepass does not account for the fade, so a place the fade emptied can keep occluding the semi-transparency behind it. And a surface faded away still casts its shadow — the shadow is drawn from the light, not the camera, and that pass has no camera distance to measure. When you fade something out completely at distance, switch the renderer's shadow settings off with it.
documents.s: Alpha Fades — make a surface disappear with distance or with angle

documents.t: Gradation LUT was added to Base Surface. It re-maps the Base Map's colours through per-channel R/G/B ramps. Assign a horizontal ramp texture to Gradation LUT and import it as sRGB. Gradation Strength sets how far the ramp result is mixed over the source colour. It is off by default, and off reads no ramp texture at all. Hue Rotation Space was added in the same place. It picks which space the base map's HSVG hue (H) rotates in. OKLab turns the hue while holding lightness and chroma steady, so moving a skin or hair colour stays predictable; HSV is the behaviour you have had so far. An existing material picks its space automatically from the HSVG values it has stored. A material already dialled in under HSV stays on HSV and its colour does not change. Use OKLab when you rotate a hue from scratch.
documents.s: Gradation LUT and Hue Rotation Space

documents.t: New Managers enable the preference by default, but builds carry the light only when the Depth master and at least one actual depth effect are enabled. Avatars with no depth features omit it automatically; authors targeting a world or host that supplies depth can turn it off manually. VRChat and WARUDO use the same setting and decision, while the scene, source prefab, and material values are preserved after the build. The generated depth light is carried as Not Important (ForceVertex), so it does not render a shadow map or ForwardAdd. This is measured in the editor; the actual VRChat client remains unverified. Existing uploads must be re-uploaded to receive it. Changes
documents.s: Shared Build Depth Light for VRChat and WARUDO

documents.t: The whole VRChat Expressions install block is gone from the Manager: Non-Destructive Modular Avatar Install, the Full/Lightweight choice behind Use Full Control Menu, Place Directly In Expressions Root, the install button, and the bulk button that switched Use VRC Runtime Controls and Switch Shadow Projection From FX on or off across every material on the character. The MingToon core package no longer builds Expressions menus, parameters or FX layers directly on an avatar. That role moved to the separate Ming Light Controller (MLC) product. Without MLC only automatic menu generation is unavailable; you can still drive the same properties with a menu and animations you author yourself. Anything installed by an earlier release stays on the avatar. The path that used to remove it is gone as well, so clean it up by hand if you no longer want it. The material's Use VRC Runtime Controls and VRC Quality Tier are still in the inspector. MLC can connect them to an avatar menu, or you can author the required menu and animations yourself without MLC. The clean-up is finished within this release: the old installer sources (MingVrcVirtualLightExpressionInstaller, MingVrcVirtualLightContract, MingVrcModularAvatarBridge) and the Manager install-panel strings are gone from the package too. The properties that Use VRC Runtime Controls keeps live through the bake, and the shader properties themselves, are unchanged; MLC drives them.
documents.s: 5. VRChat Expressions menu authoring moved to the MLC add-on

documents.t: MingToonManager's public UseModularAvatarVrcIntegration, VrcFullExpressionMenu and VrcMenuAtExpressionsRoot properties and the three serialized fields behind them are gone. They are leftovers from the built-in VRChat installer removed above, and nothing in this release reads them. Whatever a scene or prefab had stored disappears with them, but the installer itself is gone, so neither behaviour nor look changes. A user script referencing those properties will fail to compile; remove the reference. The same pass deleted MingVrcDepthAvailabilityPolicy from the package. The type held one boolean and one sentence, and nothing read either. The ship-time depth decision is still made by MingVrcDepthLightPolicy and the build depth light path, so behaviour is unchanged.
PBR Surface, Toon Specular and Region Mask were mixed into the character group and are now a separate one. It sits after Character and before Depth Effects. Values and defaults are unchanged.
documents.s: 6. Three PBR-related sections moved out into their own PBR group

documents.t: The top-level Rim group is now Stylized Lighting, reflecting that it also contains Front Light and Shadow Interior Reflection. The lighting controls moved into a Shadow section inside Basic Settings, ordered Form Shadow → Cast Shadow → Shadow Color → Shadow Pattern. The rim family reads Rim Light → Rim Shade → Front Light → Backlight → Shadow Interior Reflection, and the depth family Depth Effects Master → 2D Rim Light → 2D Translucency → 2D Shadow → Inner Outline. Fresnel-style regions now share Width, Softness, and Invert Area. Width 0 is none and 1 makes the whole domain available. Softness changes only the feather ratio inside that support without moving its outer boundary; Width 1 with Softness 1 is a full-domain gradient rather than a solid fill. Rim Light and Shadow Interior Reflection now call their former Light Direction Influence control Light-Side Emphasis, matching its actual brightness role. The old 0.5 floor on the opposite side is removed, so rotating the resolved main or Virtual Light produces an immediate response. Rim placement remains under View Alignment. Front Light is now separate from the Fresnel family and uses a dedicated circular cap whose Area Size closely tracks projected radius. It directly exposes Area Size and Softness; Light Direction Influence and the new View Direction Influence independently weight the main-light and camera directions. At a View value of 0, camera orbit leaves the cap locked to the light axis. A low-cost Highlight Core Size/Intensity reuses the same radius. Size 1 makes the full front available while Softness remains active across it. Fresnel area inversion is not used. The former Front Light Border, AreaInvert, Directivity, and ViewStrength properties were removed without automatic conversion. The new view control uses _FrontLightViewDirectionInfluence rather than reviving the old ID. New defaults and factory presets were authored for the correct mechanism; at the time of this entry the material property schema was 15 and the preset schema 10. Later changes in the same release took the material property schema to 17, which is the figure this release ships. The five former Power/Falloff values were also removed without migration instead of remaining as hidden compatibility storage. Backlight keeps its serialized Border and displays Width = 1 - Border in the inspector. 2D Rim Light gained an optional Fresnel region. It multiplies the existing 2D Rim Light result, and disabling it reproduces the previous output exactly. Invert Area bypasses only the geometric silhouette guard that would erase the camera-facing selection; depth comparison and material masks remain active.
documents.s: 7. Inspector sections and Fresnel regions cleaned up

documents.t: The number may read lower than before without you changing anything. The material did not change, the yardstick did. What actually uploads is the baked shader, so that is the headline figure now. The figure for the material you are editing is still there under the detail breakdown.
documents.s: 8. The Performance Cost meter shows the post-bake figure by default

documents.t: Leaving Pattern Style on Overlay and switching Pattern Target to Depth2D now shows a notice. Overlay prints line work over finished shading, so it only works on the form shadow; on 2D it falls back to Recolor. That has always been the case, but nothing said so.
documents.s: 9. A notice on the Overlay + Depth2D combination

documents.t: Cast Edge Feather Quality went from five kernels to three: Light3Tap, Standard5Tap and High9Tap, all one method now — a centre tap plus a golden-angle disc rotated per pixel by noise. The old per-kernel radius caps (8/20/48 px) went with them, so all three tiers honour the full slider range. Projection Feather Radius was re-based from screen pixels onto the same camera-stable world width the 2D Rim Light uses. The range went from 0-400 (default 60) to 0-20 (default 3.5). Both saved values convert automatically when the material is opened. The value you see is converted, not reset. Quality maps as Premium25Tap and SoftBilinear9Tap → High9Tap; Fast5Tap, Smooth13Tap and StableVogel5Tap → Standard5Tap; DerivativeEdgeAA1Tap → Light3Tap. The radius converts from the pixel reach each retired tier could actually produce. The number in each name is the per-pixel read count. It is the one centre read the shader already holds plus 2, 4 or 8 disc taps, and the disc reads the main directional light's shadow map only. It never reads the camera depth texture, so this control cannot bring a depth prepass along with it. The disc taps got cheaper on URP. With the project's soft shadows on, every disc tap used to unfold a 5x5 filter of its own, taking the per-pixel shadow-map reads to 36 at Standard5Tap and 72 at High9Tap. Each disc tap is now one hardware comparison, so it is 4 and 8. The disc is itself the filter that softens the edge, so laying a filter over it was doing the same job at nine times the price. The centre tap uses the filtered shadow value URP has already computed, so the softness of soft shadows stays. A setup on screen-space shadows was one fetch per tap to begin with and is unchanged, and Built-in is unchanged. The edge can come out very slightly crisper. The Performance Cost meter counts this feather now. Until now the module read as 0 on the meter, so it could not be put beside the 2D shadow, whose per-pixel reads were counted honestly. Turning the feather on and off now actually moves the number. It follows the same convention as every other module - counted only while Shadow Projection and Projection Feather are on and the radius and strength are above 0 - and the tap count is the 2, 4 or 8 of the tier you picked. Shadow-map reads are counted apart from depth reads, so the depth-prepass entry does not rise by mistake.
