documents.s: Projection Feather reworked, with automatic conversion

documents.t: Everything the inspector showed as 2D Depth Rim or Depth Rim is now labelled 2D Rim Light. Sub-entries follow the same head, so 2D Depth Rim Mask becomes 2D Rim Light Mask, and names that were missing the prefix, such as Depth Rim Backlight Boost, gain it. This entry is a label change only. No 2D Rim Light material property was renamed - _DepthRimEnabled, _DepthRimMask, _DepthRimWidth and the rest keep their identifiers - so this rename by itself needs no rebinding. A separate property-ID canonicalization does ship in this release, though: read the _Ming prefix item in the upgrade warnings above.
documents.s: 2D Depth Rim is now labelled 2D Rim Light

documents.t: Buttons that need Mask Maker, Face SDF Studio, or Ming Light Controller stay visible and stay clickable without the add-on. Clicking one opens the manual page for that feature, which is also where the purchase link lives. Each spot used to behave differently. The mask authoring button and the vertex paint start buttons were greyed out, so the reason was only visible on hover, and the Face SDF button raised a dialog and left you where you started. Master Adjust and Virtual Light follow a different rule, because they are places that write values rather than buttons. Without Ming Light Controller the rows MLC owns - the Everything That Adds Light, Of Those, Only The Silhouette, Every Shadow and Final Output groups, plus the Virtual Light group - are not drawn. No lock notice, no greyed-out control, nothing in their place: a control you cannot commit a value with is not worth showing. The Performance Distance group at the bottom of the Master Adjust tab works without the add-on, so it is always drawn. In a project without MLC it is the only group left on that tab. Either way, values already stored on the material stay where they are and the shader keeps reading them. Installing MLC brings the rows back in the same place.
documents.s: One behaviour for every button that needs a separately sold add-on

documents.t: How a cast shadow darkens a surface was rewritten. Shadow attenuation now multiplies the direct-light term only, and the ambient (SH) light is added back on top as a floor. Cast Indirect Lift, which was dead in Unified Shadow mode, works again, so a cast shadow no longer punches to black in a brightly lit environment. In a scene with no ambient it adds nothing. Materials on Unified Shadow, the shipping default, get brighter cast shadows in a scene with ambient light. The old opacity reduction used by Layer mode is replaced by the same additive floor. The point at which Suppress Backlit Silhouette starts erasing the cast shadow now follows the form shadow's effective boundary instead of a fixed angle. The new Backlit Suppression Offset (0-1, default 0.25) sets how far past that boundary, toward the dark side, the erase begins; half of 1st Shadow Blur is added on top, so the cast shadow's fade-out edge always hides inside the form shadow. It sits under Advanced on the Cast Shadow tab, directly below Suppress Backlit Silhouette. Materials with the form shadow off keep the old fixed window. The caster push behind Suppress Self Cast Shadow now fades automatically under backlight to protect the contact silhouette, and applies to directional lights only. Only materials with that toggle on are affected, and the bias is not applied under spot or point lights.

The face-only self-surface suppression row that sat on the Face tab is gone. One value now does that job - Receiver Depth Pushback on the 2D Shadow tab - and the face and the body share it. It pushes the camera depth this material writes backward to cut self-surface artifacts; 2D Shadow and SSAO Enabled read it, while the light shadow map is left unchanged. It works regardless of Face 2D Shadow Assist. It used to apply only while the assist was on, so with the assist off, which is the shipping default, the slider visible in the inspector was silently dead and angular chunks of shadow were left along the nose ridge. It now takes effect whenever All Effects and the Depth Effects Master are on and either 2D Shadow or SSAO Enabled is on. A view-facing weight was added. Only relief turned toward the camera - the nose, the cheeks, the brow - is pushed back and loses its self-artifacts, while grazing surfaces such as the underside of the jaw keep their true depth, so the chin-to-neck shadow keeps its separation. Open your materials and check Receiver Depth Pushback on the 2D Shadow tab. Use it on receiving face and body materials only and keep casters such as hair and clothing at 0. A new material defaults to 0, and the bundled factory looks use 0.01 on the face slot alone. The slider's ceiling came down from 1 to 0.1. 0.1 is 10 cm, and that is where the effect ends: the gap the 2D shadow judges front-from-back with clamps at 10 cm and the SSAO radius is far smaller, so a value above it never changed a pixel. The slider now ends where the effect ends, the same tidying this release did to the 2D Shadow Bias scale. The range anyone actually used - 0 by default, 0.01 on the factory face - is untouched, so nothing looks different. A material holding a value above 0.1 draws the same result, and moving the slider once settles it at the new ceiling.
documents.s: The face-only self-surface suppression row folded into one Receiver Depth Pushback

documents.t: The exclusion that removed the cast shadow inside the face area while Face 2D Shadow Assist was on is gone. Turning the assist on used to make scene shadows vanish from the face alone; the cast shadow and the 2D shadow now both draw there. The frontal-light self-shadow the exclusion was hiding is cancelled at its source instead. On Built-in the face's shadow-map entry is peeled along the light by the same amount, over the same area, under the same conditions as the camera-depth push (directional lights only), so the self comparison cannot succeed by construction. External casters such as a hand or a hat keep their true depths and land on the face normally. URP samples the shadow map at the rasterized position and never had the artifact. The inspector warning that had lost its basis - Face 2D Shadow Assist requires Shadow Projection and the Enable Shadow Projection button beside it - was removed. Picking 2D Shadow (Face Corrected) under Shadow Mode no longer forces Shadow Projection on either; that choice leaves the projection master alone.
documents.s: Face correction and the cast shadow now coexist

documents.t: The value now reads like an HDR intensity. It is an absolute ceiling on the final output peak with every additive effect included: at 1 the layers brighten up to just under a bloom threshold of 1 and never trip it, at 1.1 the bloom picks them up. It used to be a multiple of the base color's brightness applied to the whole final color, which erased glitter and rims outright on black clothing, and raising it released the scene light along with them and blew out to white. The same value now limits the scene-light intensity that drives those effects. At 1 only intensity up to 1 reaches rims, backlight, front light, translucency, MatCaps, emission and glitter; at 3, up to 3. That is what stops those layers burning white under a high-intensity directional light. The stored number is unchanged but its meaning is not, so brightness changes. The picture moves toward additive effects staying visible on black clothing, and toward being held back under strong lighting. Turning Bound Added Light Too off removes both limits. Exposure of the scene light itself still belongs to Maximum Final Brightness, as before.
documents.s: Added Light Brightness Maximum re-based on HDR semantics

documents.t: SSAO gained Color Purity (0-10, default 1), Color Brightness and Color Gamma; purity 1 preserves the composed color. The Unified Shadow Chroma slider still spans 0-10. The old SSAO Saturation name is not a shader property. The Color Purity on Rim Light, Backlight, Front Light, Shadow Interior Reflection, 2D Rim Light and 2D Translucency shares the same 0-10 range. 0 is grayscale, 1 is the composed color as-is, and above 1 oversaturates. Only the ceiling moved, so a stored value means what it meant before and the look is unchanged.

The MingToon menu moved out from under Tools to a top-level StudioRaming > MingToon. Paths written as Tools / Studio Raming / MingToon … elsewhere in this document are under the new root now. Every context menu is under a single MingToon root: MingToon > Add MingToon Manager and MingToon > Create Look Preset From Character in the Hierarchy, MingToon > MingToon Manager, MingToon > Ming Light Controller and MingToon > Create Look Preset From Prefab in the Project window. Right-clicking a prefab in the Project window and choosing MingToon > MingToon Manager attaches the Manager without opening the prefab in a scene. It handles a multiple selection, and imported model roots such as an FBX are skipped with the reason stated. Ming Light Controller moved to StudioRaming > Ming Light Controller > Open and > Avatar Attachment. The same path used to be both a leaf and a submenu, which hid the main window.

The experimental Face Proxy Depth feature is gone. It was compiled out by default in both shaders with no way to switch it on, so nothing renders differently. Its four properties left the shaders, so the material property schema moved to 15 and the generated shader cache version moved up with it. Later changes in the same release raised both numbers further, so this entry alone does not decide either one. What this release finally ships is material property schema 17 and generated shader cache version 66; Release/MingToon_ReleaseManifest.json is the authority. The re-bake described above covers this too.

The Tools / Studio Raming / MingToon / VRChat Preview menu documented in 0.1.5 is gone. Its three surfaces - Authoring, VRChat - no camera depth, VRChat - camera depth available - are no longer available and nothing replaces them. The menu path did not move, so there is nothing to look for. To check whether depth is actually being supplied, set Depth Sampling > Depth Availability to Diagnostic in the material inspector; it paints the detection state on screen.

The colour and intensity of additional lights - point and spot - are added thinly into the Fresnel rim. Until now the rim answered the main light alone, so a silhouette edge stayed the main light's colour even in a scene lit from the side by a coloured lamp. A material with Enable Fresnel Rim on gets a different edge colour in a scene with additional lights. How much is added is bound to Rim Light's colour and Blend Opacity, so several lights together still do not blow out to white. Nothing is added on a material with Enable Fresnel Rim off or Intensity at 0, and the whole thing drops out in Performance Distance's far band. It reads no extra texture. On URP the Fresnel rim used to take additional lights twice; it now matches BRP. Both backends multiply by the main light and add the additional ones, one way only. A URP material gets a different rim colour in a scene with additional lights.
documents.s: Point and spot lights now reach Rim Light

documents.t: The value stored in the bundled presets came down from 10 to 1. When the purity ceiling was widened to 0-10 the preset values were saved pinned to that ceiling, so applying a factory look pushed the rim colour into oversaturation. 1 means the composed colour as-is, the same as the shader default. It takes effect only when you apply a preset again. A value already stored on a material you made is left alone.
documents.s: The factory looks' Rim Light > Color Purity default is now 1

documents.t: Applying a Look Preset, saving a preset and applying a JSON document all work regardless of the version stored on the material. Those three paths used to refuse an older material with an error telling you to run the project migration first. That check, the error and the dialog that offered to run the migration are all gone. The official path from 0.1.6 is to delete the Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon folder and import 0.1.7 fresh. So many property names changed that old values do not carry over, so dial your materials back in from the new defaults and use a Look Preset if you want to get there faster. Bake output has to be baked again too. Nothing in the product requires the migration any more. Improvements
documents.s: A material's version no longer blocks presets and JSON

documents.t: The more MatCap layers a material stacks, the bigger the difference. You can see it on the Performance Cost meter once you rebake. Materials that do not use MatCap are unchanged. Materials you upload to VRChat and WARUDO now cost the same as they do on URP. Until now an identically configured material was heavier on the Built-in side alone.
documents.s: 10. Avatars that use MatCap get lighter

documents.t: The workspace bar has five tabs. Optimize contains texture optimization and per-type resolution caps; automatic build and play-mode hooks are configured in Upload. Analyze in Optimize produces four suggestions for this avatar: bake materials with identical settings as one, fold uniform textures into constants, pack mask textures together, and switch off modules that have no effect. All are off by default. Choices are remembered per avatar in this computer's user settings. Expand the material selection tools below the workspace bar to use All, Face, Face & Skin, Common and Exclude Face. Overview starts with the current avatar state and next action. Expand the estimated-spec card to see material slots, estimated draw calls (authoring and baked), the highest texture-binding count, the highest per-pixel depth read count, texture memory and the VRChat performance rank those imply. These are estimates; the SDK build panel remains the source of the final numbers. The same screen toggles Depth Effects, 2D Shadow, Enable SSAO, Cast Shadow and Outline across the whole avatar at once, with undo.
documents.s: An Optimize tab, an estimated-spec card and a material selection row in the Manager

documents.t: Transparent Draw Order was added to 3 · Details on the Manager's Look & Bake tab. Transparent parts are drawn in order of distance from the camera, but an avatar's skinned meshes usually share one large bounds, so every part reports the same distance. Sorting Order alone then decides, and parts left on the same value are tied — which is how a ribbon ends up behind the blouse it belongs on top of. Find Parts With Undecided Order collects the groups distance cannot separate, listed per shared material. Order them yourself with ▲▼ in the list; up is behind, down is in front. Left unordered, Unity picks between them arbitrarily, and the choice can change every time the scene is reopened or the avatar is built.
documents.s: Transparent Draw Order in the Manager

documents.t: Matcap layers that only add and carry no mask are merged into a single map at bake time; the layer count and its keyword come down with them. A texture slot that is empty, or whose texels are all one colour, folds into a constant - the sample and the binding disappear together. A material with outlines authored off no longer submits the outline hull pass, as long as nothing animates its outline properties. That is one pass fewer per slot. Depth Effect Mask and Outline Width Mask join the existing mask pack, two textures fewer. All of it needs a rebake to apply.
documents.s: The bake removes more textures and draw calls

documents.t: Simple was reorganised into 6 groups and 22 sections. Form Shadow, Normal Outline, Face Shading, Depth Effects - Common, Inner 2D Edge and SSAO moved into Simple; Master Adjust, Stencil and Glitter moved out to Full. Simple keeps every section and shows only the values that actually get adjusted. Face Border now displays on the same normalized 0-1 scale as the body border and is mirrored into the Form Shadow tab for face materials. Edge Rim Minimum Multiplier was added to Master Adjust; a material seen for the first time opens only Quick Settings and leaves the other sections collapsed. 2D Shadow Bias was also capped from 10 to 1. The ? button on a section header opens the matching page of the online documentation in the inspector's language. 33 sections map onto 22 pages, and the Manager and the Validator warnings link the same way. Property tooltips were expanded considerably. The share of inspector-visible shader properties carrying a tooltip went from 30.7% to 41.8% (160 more), all three languages filled in. The Manager has five tabs: Overview, Setup, Look & Bake, Upload and Optimize. Overview shows current status and the actual next action; Setup owns conversion inputs; Look & Bake reapplies the look after conversion and rebakes while preserving selected scope and options; Upload runs the normal automatic path, checks the current avatar, then exposes advanced manual bake; Optimize owns project optimization without a duplicate automatic-hook instruction. Section headers went from 34 to 22 points tall and the gap between sections narrowed. The master toggle is a checkbox instead of a pill whose width moved with its label, and the ?, favourite and reset icons line up across every section. Collapse All and Expand All are in the inspector's top bar and in the pinned bar both. Collapsing leaves the workflow group banners open, so the list of closed tabs reads at a glance. The pinned bar gained a Changed Only view, the cost grade with the module driving it, workflow group jump buttons, and a row naming the section you are currently inside (clicking it collapses that section). The bug that stopped the bar following the scroll at 200% scaling is fixed too.
documents.s: The inspector and the Manager, tidied

documents.t: VRC Light Volumes (Test) is an in-editor preview toggle. A VRChat avatar upload turns the module on regardless of the value, reading the Light Volumes the world placed instead of Unity light probes, and the value stored on the material is restored once the upload finishes. In a world without volumes it falls back to probes and the picture is unchanged. A world build turns it on only when the scene actually holds a Light Volume component. Turning it on in the editor compiles one more variant and adds a Texture3D read, so enable it only to preview the look in a volume world. Built-in only; the row does not appear on a URP material.
documents.s: VRC Light Volumes turn on automatically for an upload

documents.t: Development console logs are stripped from the C# sources that go into the package. 27 lines - shader warm-up progress, internal bake tags and the like - no longer appear. Not one warning or error was removed, and the logs that report the result of something you asked for stay as well.

Switching a baked material's shader back to the editable one by hand leaves the MatCap atlas values behind with no per-layer maps. The MatCap Layers tab now opens with a yellow warning at the top: "This material still carries the bake-only MatCap atlas values, so the MatCap layers look empty. Use the original material, or bake it again." There is no automatic repair, because guessing the maps back would be inventing content. Restore the recorded editable material or bake again. Restore, cleanup, the backend swap and migration all leave a baked copy's shader alone, so no normal path raises this warning.
documents.s: A warning on a material left holding bake-only MatCap values

documents.t: When Performance Distance (m) times Performance Distance Scale is 0, the material renders at its lightest tier at every distance and the camera-depth effects, PBR, the extra matcap and normal layers, toon specular, glitter and screen tone never draw. The validator now reports that as MING-MAT-PERF-DISTANCE-ZERO. It is a warning, not an error. Zero is a legal authored value and the end MLC drives the scale down to in game, so a material parked there on purpose is fine as it is; otherwise the message points you at Performance Distance Scale on the Master Adjust tab.
documents.s: The validator catches a material with a performance distance of zero

documents.t: The bulk edit panel that changes several materials at once gained a Base Map Opacity row. The mask authoring button now supports the blend mask slots on emission layers 1 and 2. Those two were the only slots left off the list. Seven slots the per-type texture resolution caps could not classify - Reflection Color / Mask, Reflection Cubemap, Gradation LUT and the MatCap and emission mask slots - were put in their place. Those textures no longer stay at their source resolution when a cap is set. Outline Master was registered in the module list. The retired properties _DepthShadowDistanceReach, _SsaoQuality and _SsaoFarDistance were missing from the retired list, so the values stored on a material were never cleaned up. Migrate Project To Current Schema now clears them with the rest. That command is optional, and a leftover value does not affect the look.
documents.s: Entries that were missing from a list

documents.t: The install wait now covers only the variants a default scene needs on first paint (the predicted first-paint requests plus the recorded variants that match that lighting) and hands the editor back the moment they land. Everything else keeps compiling behind the Progress window on the same asynchronous job, which is not gated on editor focus. The stall window is longer, so a slow cold first compile is no longer misread as a stall and dropped to the serial compile path. A conversion's prewarm joins the running asynchronous job instead of the focus-gated runner. Conversion skips the mesh bake stage entirely when no mesh channel is checked, and the re-pin/save step shows its own progress text.
documents.s: The post-install / post-conversion warm-up wait ends at the first-paint set

documents.t: Every Face preset now uses Softness 0.001. The three presets with the 2D shadow enabled set Receiver Depth Pushback and Depth Stretch to 0, keep Face 2D Shadow Assist off, and use a 2D Shadow Bias of 0.15. This applies only to presets you apply from now on; existing materials are untouched. Bug fixes
documents.s: 2D shadow values of the factory Face look presets

documents.t: It now moves across smoothly. This affects every material using an SDF face.
documents.s: 11. Face shading snapped hard as the light crossed the centre of the face

documents.t: On a unified material with the face vertex-painted, shadows falling on the body sat away from where they belonged. It now applies to the face only.
documents.s: 12. A depth offset meant for the face alone pushed the body with it

documents.t: You had to restart the editor before you could rebake. It rebakes immediately now.
documents.s: 13. Deleting a bake output and baking again failed

documents.t: Those two rows were missing from the inspector entirely, so unlike the first slot there was no way to pick a channel. Both slots match now.
documents.s: 14. You could not choose Channel Source or Invert Source Colors on the second emission slot

documents.t: Two preset scope toggles were clipped in Korean and Japanese, leaving them unreadable — Overwrite Shadow Colors Too and Overwrite Fresnel Too are now split across two lines. Narrowing the inspector clipped the sliders and number fields in the middle, so you could not type a value — the value column survives at narrow widths now. The revert button sat outside its row's box with too much margin on the right — it now sits inside the box it belongs to.
If you do not read Korean there was no way back to English or Japanese. It follows the system language now.
documents.s: 16. Opening Face SDF Studio first locked the MingToon inspector to Korean as well

documents.t: Even when the proxy centre is placed in front of the face, the target normal now stays within the visible face hemisphere. Removed the separate planar-normal blend called Normal Method. Proxy Normal Intensity is now the only blend between the original and proxy-shaped normals. Proxy radius now controls actual normal curvature. Smaller sphere, cylinder and capsule proxies bend normals more strongly; larger ones transition more gently. The top-left Scene view panel can independently toggle normal lines and the proxy volume, while display length and density remain independent from rendered lighting. Materials using a texture face-region mask now preview normal lines with the actual UV, channel, inversion, and remapping. If the mask cannot be sampled, the tool hides misleading lines and reports why.
documents.s: 17. Face proxy normals flipped under front lighting or reacted over an unnaturally narrow angle

documents.t: The VRChat face-normal bake isolates build-only Face slots with temporary materials. It does not mutate the scene's original Meshes and materials or materials shared by another avatar. For each face-normal optimization build root, it first records the original Mesh and material slots of every Renderer that has a Mesh. Recovery restores even non-Face Renderer Meshes replaced by a later upload conversion, and resumes journal and temporary-material ownership recovery across script reloads or editor restarts. Regular conversion records Renderers, Meshes, materials, Prefab overrides, and dirty state before each mutation. Its journal is written atomically under ProjectSettings; a backup repairs a damaged primary file, and an older Library journal is migrated once. After eight failed automatic recovery attempts, retry from the Advanced menu or inspect the pending work before discarding only the recovery journal.
documents.s: 18. Upload and conversion recovery is now interruption-safe

documents.t: When a build was interrupted and its material was deleted afterwards, the recovery could never complete - yet it retried on every domain reload and printed a fresh red error each time, so it appeared on every script recompile and every entry into Play mode. The first attempt now waits for the import to finish, and only records whose material is gone from the project are dropped, once, with their names. Only after three failed attempts does it name the materials still waiting and what to do about them, in a single warning, and then it stays quiet. A recovery failure during a build or an upload still stops the build as before.
documents.s: Startup recovery is incomplete repeated on every editor start

documents.t: On a pixel where normal layers were stacked inverted and at full strength, the math could overflow and drop the whole normal stack. The same limit in the direction vectors the 2D Shadow and the 2D Rim Light use is fixed with it. Where the tangent is near zero, BRP and URP built different tangent frames, and the 2D Shadow's depth-placement fallback pointed forward on one backend and backward on the other. Both now use the same expression on both. The first two are defensive fixes that only surface on a GPU that really runs half precision; the last two were a BRP/URP result difference that showed on PC as well. Verified through the shader compile gate; not verified in a live render.
documents.s: Four precision and backend-mismatch fixes in the normal and depth math

documents.t: Unticking a region and applying left the slot it had already written in place, so a region applied once could not be removed with the tool. Apply now writes all four slots, and a region left off is actually removed from the material. The window does not read the material's current values. Applying an empty window over a material whose stack, normal or MatCap slots are already filled clears those slots, so set the window's regions up before applying. Undo (Ctrl+Z) works.
documents.s: Regions could not be taken back out in the One Slot / Tiled Regions window

documents.t: The module's shader keyword was declared on neither BRP nor URP, so switching it on applied no ramp and the whole thing dropped out of the compile. It works now. A material that already had Gradation LUT on looks different. The ramp that was ignored until now is applied to the base colour. Switch the row off if you need the old picture. On a material using UV scrolling, rotation or atlas animation, Built-in alone skipped the ramp; that is fixed with it. It needs a rebake to apply.
documents.s: Turning Gradation LUT on did nothing

documents.t: Render Disabled (do not draw this material) now blocks the screen draw and removes depth/shadow passes at the vertex stage on both Built-in and URP. Hidden materials no longer write camera depth or the light shadow map, so they do not cast 2D shadows, SSAO contact, or projected shadows. Older hidden materials are healed on next selection or project migration.
documents.s: Render Disabled could not switch the transparent depth prepass off

documents.t: MingToon > Create Look Preset From Prefab in the Project window wrote every unsaved change in the project to disk at save time. It now saves only the preset asset it actually created or overwrote.
documents.s: Creating a look preset from a prefab saved unrelated work with it

documents.t: The preview read its own temporary material, decided there was no face, and never built the data to draw the normal lines from at all. It now judges from the original material's values.
documents.s: The face proxy Scene view preview was never built

documents.t: The conversion wrote the emission map and mask fresh but left Channel Source, Invert Source Colors and the blend mask's channel and inversion at the pre-conversion material's values, so either emission layer could come out different from the original. The conversion now resets those values with the rest.
documents.s: lilToon conversion left the emission channel settings at their old values

documents.t: A configuration that locked a Photo Look Bit to a fixed value was refused at the install step with a "no target binding" error. Fixed.
documents.s: Ming Light Controller — a configuration with a Photo Look Bit pinned was refused at install

documents.t: If you connect an external or shared Face SDF map while Face SDF Studio has an automatic refresh waiting, it checks the connection again just before applying the older automatic job so that job does not overwrite your map.
documents.s: Preserve a map changed manually while Face SDF auto refresh is pending

documents.t: The cleanup checks every material contained in one asset file and changes it to the current shader. It first checks that the material can be saved, then reads the saved reference again after the change. If it cannot save or verify the result, it leaves the existing generated profile and keeps the cleanup incomplete.
documents.s: Verify material references when cleaning up 0.1.6 generated profiles

documents.t: Turning off automatic camera settings in the Inspector removes the settings that automation applied. When you use an existing post-processing layer, it does not overwrite the layer mask and volume trigger settings you changed later.
documents.s: Disable automatic camera settings without overwriting later settings

documents.t: The shader variant's compilation errors are checked after it is warmed up. A variant with an error is not recorded as ready, and the failure reason is reported.
documents.s: A compile failure was recorded as a completed warmup

documents.t: When the original mask and settings saved in the project match, the same mask pack is reused after reopening the Editor. Existing packs are neither deleted nor renamed, so the first application of this change can create one new pack.
documents.s: Reuse the same mask pack after restarting the Editor

documents.t: The baked profile of a material that uses an alpha mask or a region mask failed to compile on D3D11, so the build hook left that material on the editable shader for the upload. That put every variant of the editable shader into the avatar bundle and made the upload about five minutes longer. Avatars that are already uploaded need a re-upload to receive this fix.
documents.s: Baked shaders of materials with an alpha mask or region mask failed to compile

documents.t: When no mesh channel was checked and the mesh bake was skipped, the conversion itself finished but building the completion dialog title threw a NullReferenceException. Fixed.
documents.s: NullReferenceException in the conversion completion dialog

documents.t: Fixes re-published without a version bump are listed round by round on the 0.1.7 Hotfix page.

0.1.7 hotfix · the package version stays 0.1.7 How to read a hotfix A hotfix is the same 0.1.7 package uploaded again without a version bump. Download it again from BOOTH and overwrite Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon. To see which round your package contains, check the entries in Docs/PATCH_NOTES_0.1.7.md inside the package. New rounds are always added at the top of this page.

After updating The face proxy needs nothing beyond the overwrite. Open the scene and the editable material's proxy normal is computed by the shader right away. No re-upload is needed. A material converted from a lilToon source with no outline that relies on stencil needs a re-conversion or the Outline > Stencil Settings matched to the surface values by hand. A material with Enable Emission on needs a re-conversion or one press of Sync Fallback Properties in the Manager, then a re-upload, before its VRChat fallback turns black. A project whose VRChat build was stuck on Material recovery is incomplete cleans itself up after one editor restart following the overwrite. lilToon-converted materials that rely on stencil (eye overlays, hidden-mesh masks) need a re-conversion or the stencil values set back by hand. No re-upload is needed.

Symptom — a tuned proxy snapped back to the original normals at every scene save, Play mode, reload or validation, and meanwhile the inspector pointed at a preview clone so edits never reached the source material. Fix — the temporary UV7 preview mesh and material swap is gone. On the editable material the shader computes the proxy normal itself. The upload copy is still baked from the proxy settings as before, and that material compiles the live path out. Live and baked use the same math. Also fixed — on a Skinned Mesh Renderer with a Root Bone the Proxy Area Mask center landed off the face. The shader's object space there is the root bone's (usually Hips), so the editor now publishes a per-renderer correction.
documents.s: Face proxy normals kept "coming undone" in the scene

documents.t: Symptom — an eye stencilled to show through the fringe showed through on the surface while its outline stayed hidden behind the hair. lilToon variants without an outline carry unused outline stencil values, and the outline MingToon draws after conversion received that neutral unit. Fix — when the source draws no outline, the outline inherits the surface stencil unit. A source that draws its own outline keeps its own values as before.
documents.s: Converting a lilToon material with no outline left its outline ignoring the stencil mask

documents.t: Symptom — an avatar dropped to the fallback by a shader block or a failed shader load came out white with only its outline left. The fallback _EmissionColor carried the tint × intensity of any material with Enable Emission on, and the VRChat fallback shaders add that colour over the whole surface when no emission map is set. Fix — the fallback emission alias is now always black. MingToon's own emission is unchanged.
documents.s: The VRChat fallback shader painted the whole avatar white with the emission colour

documents.t: Symptom — after one build of an avatar that uses NDMF, every later VRChat build failed with Material recovery is incomplete. Fix — recovery records for the clone materials NDMF creates under Packages/nadena.dev.ndmf/__Generated/ and deletes after the build stayed in the journal. The missing-material check now looks at the file on disk instead of the GUID mapping alone, and such records are cleared at the next recovery with a single warning.
documents.s: Stale NDMF clone records kept blocking the VRChat build

documents.t: Symptom — the lilToon conversion carries the source stencil unit across (Ref, Comp, Pass and so on), but the factory look applied right after it held the shader defaults (Ref 0, Always, Keep), so the stencil that eye overlays and hidden-mesh masks rely on went back to 0. Re-applying a look did the same. Fix — both stencil units (surface and outline, 14 properties) are now neither captured into nor written by a preset.
documents.s: Look presets overwrote the stencil values

documents.t: Open Beta · 2026-09-08
Permanent link: 0.1.8 patch notes

First-upload time — Improved the excessive time required for uploads. User measurements report a 3–50% improvement for a first upload; results vary by environment. White VRC-baked characters — In the VRC bake path, emission layers are now composed sequentially over the current lit result instead of overwriting it, addressing characters turning white after a bake and upload. Emission masks, shadow visibility, Normal/Multiply blending, map RGB/alpha, and surface alpha are retained. Re-bake and re-upload existing baked materials to receive this change. Fallback path distinction — The change that forces the fallback emission alias (_EmissionColor) to black shipped separately in the 0.1.7 HotFix1 release. This 0.1.8 fix covers emission composition in the regular MingToon bake/render path. Re-bake and re-upload baked materials created before 0.1.7 HotFix1. Ming Light Controller 0.1.1 — BRP-only projects no longer fail because a missing URP shader was validated during upload. MLC now validates each installed MingToon backend and reports an error only when neither backend is installed. Authorized transient IDs for NDMF build clones stay in memory and never rewrite the source avatar or project files. The menu's Saturation control binds to MingToon's Output Master Saturation. MLC is a separate package; update it after installing MingToon. Recovery when an older Assets installation conflicts — Only when the older Assets-based installation conflicts with the new installer and installation fails, first move any .mat, texture, or preset files saved directly inside Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon elsewhere, then delete only that MingToon folder and import again. Do not delete MingLightController or the entire StudioRaming folder. This cleanup is needed once when migrating from the older Assets installation and is not repeated for later VPM updates. Conversion stability — Fixed lilToon conversion changing SSAO color purity, disabling emission masks, or changing mask data through compression. Upload texture rewrites (opt-in) — The default LosslessOnly texture bake policy never rewrites authored texels. Enable Reviewed Texture Rewrites On Build (Opt-In) on Optimize only with Optimize On Build / Upload (Applies To Everything) enabled to flatten Texture Layers and Normal Layers before upload and pack loose masks into RGBA. Color-space conversion, regenerated mips, or platform compression can change pixels, so compare target-platform captures before and after baking; the widened pack also includes Width Mask on the Outline tab. Manager controls — Update status and installed/latest versions now fit in two rows at about one third of the previous height, with Check, Update, and Notes in one place. Installation and update paths — Import the DLL unitypackage downloaded from BOOTH to install the required MingToon package automatically without an additional install button. This is the VCC/VPM-based path introduced in this release. Unity then checks for new versions at startup and shows a notice for versions that have neither been installed nor skipped. The user must click the Update button in the notice to install; if Unity is playing, compiling, or building, it waits and checks again after reload. Restarting Unity does not install a version automatically. Skip applies only to that version, and the next new version is announced again. Users who installed through VCC continue to maintain and update it manually through VCC. Existing asset preservation — Existing 0.1.7 installations and inventories are recognized; package updates touch only managed files and preserve existing materials, scenes, prefabs, and Unity-created package.json.meta files.

Color Presets — Use the Color Presets panel to save and apply the full Shadow Color tab (bands, chroma, brightness, and color map), rim/depth tints, and HSVG. The seven factory palettes are Neutral, Warm Tone 1, Warm Tone 2, Cool Tone 1, Cool Tone 2, High Saturation, and Low Saturation. Textures outside the preset's targets, render state, and keywords stay intact; presets apply to multiple selected materials and support Undo. Band and rim color controls — Quick settings expose overall saturation and emission intensity, while SSAO Color, Rim Shade Color, and shadow-band colors can be set directly. A Rim Shade Color blend opacity of 0 preserves the existing 1st Shadow Color. Output Master Saturation — Applies to the final output: 0 is grayscale, 1 is the baseline, and values above 1 strengthen chroma while preserving brightness. Per-layer UV selection — Choose UV Source (UV0–UV3) independently for each normal layer and Mask UV Source separately for its mask. With both at UV0 (the default), the UV-router variant is not compiled.

Language display — Installation and update messages select Korean, Japanese, or English for other system languages; Manager labels continue to follow the Inspector language selection. Conversion output — Converted materials retain emission-map RGB/alpha and emission-mask RGBA data, including surface-alpha blending for transparent materials. Per-layer normal UV Source and mask Mask UV Source (UV0–UV3) choices are copied as well.

Shader baking — Identical requests are grouped to reduce duplicate work during repeated bakes while preserving existing generated output and state. Generated-output recovery — Interrupted bakes now recover without leaving partial files that can poison the next generated-shader cache. Outline normal stability — Replaced the outline normal's object-scale-sensitive geometric correction with finite, scale-invariant handling and an authored-direction fallback for degenerate or non-finite geometry.
Manager Notes opens the latest localized documentation, while the current and latest versions remain visible together.

Back up your project, then move any personal materials, textures, or presets out of Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon. For an older Assets-based installation, delete only that MingToon folder before importing the new installer. Do not delete MingLightController or the entire StudioRaming folder. This cleanup is only for migration from the older installation method, not for every subsequent VPM update.
Open Beta · September 9, 2026
This update focuses on choosing conversion looks and colors, the Manager workflow, bake stability, and generated texture optimization.

Work organized into three tabs — The tabs are Get Started, Look & Bake, and Optimize. Select your conversion targets and convert them in Get Started, then adjust the look and bake settings of existing MingToon materials in Look & Bake. Optimize contains automatic processing and texture resolution limits. The material selection and target scope at the top are shared across all three tabs. Choose looks and colors separately — Added a Color Preset selector below Look Preset. The default is Neutral. The look is applied first, followed by the selected colors. This replaces the previous shadow-color overwrite checkbox. Keep Existing Values — Select Keep Existing Values in Color Preset to retain the colors converted from the source. Previous settings that preserved shadow colors carry over to this option. Selecting a separate color preset replaces the corresponding colors with that preset's values. Preserve shadow bands — Applying a look preset during conversion no longer overwrites the shadow-band strength, boundaries, width, or blending settings taken from the source. Color preset selection and preservation of band settings are handled separately. Reapply to current MingToon materials — When only editable MingToon materials remain and there are no materials to convert, Get Started can reapply the selected look and colors to all MingToon materials on the character. A confirmation explains what will be overwritten, and Undo restores the previous values. Menus and components — Internal development diagnostics are hidden from product menus, and the manually added product components are organized around MingToon Manager and Ming Light Controller. The project validation menu remains available.
documents.s: Manager and look and color selection

documents.t: First and second shadow colors and strength — Source shadow strength, boundaries, and softness are reflected in MingToon settings. The second shadow's alpha is combined with overall shadow strength, fixing cases where the second shadow remained at zero strength or became too faint at intermediate alpha values. Additional shadow colors — The source's first shadow color is passed to other shadow settings so they do not remain white even when shadow-color unification is off. A source second shadow with zero alpha does not enable the second band. Convert the materials that can be processed — If conversion fails for some materials, the remaining materials continue to be processed. Failed slots retain their originals, and successful conversion results are kept. Problems in postprocessing, such as applying the selected look or colors, also appear in the results so you can distinguish completed, excluded, and failed items. Transparent materials — For ordinary transparent materials, the visible-surface cutoff is separated from the cutoff used for depth processing, and animated source cutoffs are preserved more reliably. Refraction materials retain their existing separate conversion path. Because the shadow calculations differ, not every lilToon look will match pixel for pixel. After conversion, check the actual appearance, including lighting and masks.

Fixed temporary baked shaders sometimes remaining on editable materials after VRChat SDK builds. Fixed cutout edges changing after baking on some alpha-masked materials, such as straps with no main texture assigned. Materials turning white after baking — Fixed an issue where emission that was turned off could be enabled during baking and cover the entire material in white. Each material's enabled or disabled state is preserved even when emission intensity or color is controlled by animation. Emission turning off or changing state — Fixed bake results so the enabled state of emission and the second emission layer is reflected correctly. Enabled layers are retained, and disabled layers are not turned on unexpectedly. Glitter applied to other materials — When converting or baking an avatar that uses Glitter on some materials, the effect could also be applied to materials with Glitter disabled. Each material now follows its own Glitter state. Glitter mask stability — Fixed an issue where a mask might not apply after a manual bake, or where region restriction might not work when the mask was enabled later. Mask inversion and color masks are also preserved. Selective preset application — After conversion or when reapplying a preset, the modules currently in use and their related settings are no longer overwritten by the preset's disabled values. The look is applied while preserving settings that must remain, rather than overwriting every preset value across the material.

Improved baking to retain optimizations for fixed material settings and reduce redundant shader variants that do not affect the result. Consolidated repeated shader calculations — Organized repeated calculations in lighting direction and overall color adjustments, and reduced unnecessary processing for unused texture layers. The focus is on lowering rendering overhead while preserving the existing look and animation control. Improved bake and upload preparation — Reduced duplicate work while checking and saving material and keyword states. The improvement varies with the avatar's composition, used features, and shader cache state. Distant MatCap display retained — Fixed an issue where colors or emission produced by MatCap disappeared when the camera moved away. Stronger save and recovery checks — Improved the accuracy of checking material save and recovery state when saving failed or work was interrupted during baking.

Resolution limits on merged results — Resolution limits apply to generated results after texture and normal layers are merged and masks are packed. Both regular masks and mask packs generated while editing materials follow the mask resolution setting. Source import settings preserved — Source textures' maximum size and compression settings are not changed to apply resolution limits or compression. No limit keeps the dimensions of the merged result. Compression and saving of generated results — Merged color and normal textures use compression for PC. Generated masks are stored losslessly to preserve channel values, with their dimensions reduced by the mask resolution limit. Cache reuse and recovery — Reduced unnecessary rewrites and imports when reusing generated results with the same settings. An existing cache is not reused unchanged when settings or output dimensions change. Files of unconfirmed origin at an output path are not overwritten or deleted without verification. Generated folders on a fresh installation — Mask output folders can now be created in projects installed from a package even when the Assets/StudioRaming folder does not exist. To regenerate textures during automatic build and upload processing, check both Optimize On Build / Upload (Applies To Everything) and Reviewed Texture Rewrites On Build (Opt-In) in the Optimize tab. Size reduction and processing time will be confirmed after validation with actual avatars; no figures are provided in these notes yet.

Exceptions during Animator analysis — When reading invalid or unusual Animator states causes an exception, the failed analysis is reported and handled conservatively. This helps avoid fixing animated values in place when analysis is incomplete. Scene view depth display recovery — Improved how depth display is requested again for the current Scene view. Play Mode and depth-display suppression settings are preserved.

Fractional Int values and the final budget gate — When the installed SDK accepts them, fractional Int defaults such as 0.5 are preserved, with a notice that integer consumers may floor or clamp them. If the final synced budget is exceeded, the build is blocked with the excess bit count and clear reduction guidance. VRCFury boundary — Full collaboration with VRCFury compression and a post-compression Inspector preview are deferred to the next version. These notes distinguish pre-compression estimates from what must be checked again during the build. MLC is a separate package. To use it with MingToon 0.1.9, update MLC to 0.1.2 as well. Supported Unity versions are 2021.3 and 2022.3; VRChat uploads must use the Unity version required by the installed SDK.

To apply the fixes to an already baked material, restore it to an editable material and bake it again. Avatars already uploaded to VRChat must be uploaded again. If you temporarily set emission intensity to 0 to avoid white rendering, adjust it to the desired value after updating and bake again. Values already changed by applying a preset in an earlier version are not restored automatically. Adjust the required settings again, or convert again from the original material and check the result. Installation and update guide · Bake and restore · 0.1.8 patch notes

Keep MingToon Manager on the root of every avatar you work on with MingToon. It manages target meshes, conversion, looks, and update checks. This guide starts with adding Manager after installation, then converting and refining materials in Quick Settings. Complete installation first. Face SDF Studio is not yet released and is not needed for this workflow.

In Hierarchy, select the root object of the avatar you are working on. Find MingToon Manager in Add Component and add it. Keep Manager on the avatar root even when working only on its outfit. Check that the target meshes are beneath this object, and work with one Manager selected. Keep the component after conversion and use it to check updates and work status. If installed through VCC, update MingToon in VCC. Check the installation method before following update guidance in Manager.
documents.s: 1. Add Manager to the avatar root first

documents.t: In Manager's Setup, assign the face mesh as Face and bare-skin meshes as Skin. Use the face and skin renderer assignment fields and check the per-slot role preview. Do not assign all eyes, eyelashes, clothing, or hair as face or skin. When converting only an outfit without a face or bare skin, leave those assignments empty. If one Renderer combines skin and clothing, separate their slot roles and keep clothing as Regular. Roles determine which materials receive the preset's face, skin, or common values. → Role assignment details
documents.s: 2. Assign Face Mesh and Skin Mesh

documents.t: Choose a starting look in Look Preset On Convert. Start with a preset close to the desired mood, then refine its values after conversion. Select None to start from imported source settings without applying a look preset.

Starting point Selection Create a new mood with preset colours Choose a tone in Color Preset Start with the original material's colours Select Keep Existing Values Keep Existing Values preserves converted source colours, shadow bands, and blending settings. It is separate from None, which disables the look preset. The colour preset applies after the look; selecting it alone does not edit materials.
documents.s: 4. Choose a colour tone or existing material values

documents.t: Check the meshes, roles, look, and colour selection, then press Convert. After completion, check that editable MingToon materials are assigned to the target. If the result lists excluded or failed slots, inspect those materials and reasons before continuing.

Select converted materials and open Quick Settings in their Inspector. Manager's material selection tools help select just the face, skin, or other materials you need. Start by adjusting face, skin, and clothing separately; select multiple materials when you want the same values on all of them. Work through colour and brightness → shadow edges → outline → rim, gloss, and emission, moving one control at a time and watching the model. Use search or Full Settings for controls absent from Quick Settings. You do not need to enable every feature below.
documents.s: 6. Refine the look in Quick Settings

documents.t: Desired change Controls to find first What to watch Overall colour Base Map HSVG Adjust hue, saturation, value, and gamma gradually; check skin and clothing Brightness in dark areas Indirect Light Lift · Minimum Final Brightness Check dark-area brightness and shading; use Preserve Base Map Color separately for lighting hue Shadow edges 1st Shadow Softness Lower for a sharper edge, higher for a softer transition Shadow colour Shadow Colour Tune skin, hair, and clothing separately Outline Outline Width · Outline Colour Check both close-up and full-body views Edge lighting Rim Light · 2D Rim Check silhouette emphasis; 2D rim also requires camera depth Surface gloss Matcap · Toon Specular Check for excessive highlights on hair and clothing Self-lit details Emission Limit it to intended areas and adjust colour and intensity If a value has no visible effect, check overall effects → the module toggle → the feature's requirements. Depth-based features such as 2D rim and 2D shadow need the setup described in Depth Effects.

Once the materials look the way you want, upload the avatar through VRC SDK or build the WARUDO mod. Automatic optimization baking runs during that workflow; a separate manual Bake is not the starting requirement. Keep MingToon Manager on the avatar root and check its automatic build/upload optimization status. See Automatic Optimization On Build and your target platform guide. See Current Limitations for the beta's verification boundaries.

MingToon 0.1.10 Open Beta core targets BRP. URP is excluded from this BRP Open Beta and included with every commercial license. After this guide, you will have a Unity project with MingToon imported without errors.

Target determines which Unity version Target Unity Rationale VRChat PC (primary target) 2022.3.22f1 Current VRChat SDK baseline Warudo 2021.3.45f2 Warudo Mod SDK 0.14.3.10 baseline General Unity 2021.3 LTS Use 2022.3.22f1 if targeting VRChat. MingToon's VRChat build hook and VRChat runtime compile only under UNITY_2022_3_OR_NEWER. On 2021.3, this code does not exist at all, so automatic optimization and VRChat-specific upload processing—including the separate Upload Depth Light opt-in—do not run. You cannot target both VRChat and Warudo with one project. Split projects by target.

Choose VCC or BOOTH on the official download page. Prepare VRChat SDK3 (Avatars) first for a VRChat project. Migrating from the older Assets installation Back up your project and exit Play mode. Move any materials, textures or presets you saved inside Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon to another folder, then delete only the old MingToon folder before installing the new package. Do not delete all of Assets/StudioRaming or the MingLightController folder. This cleanup is needed only when moving from the older Assets installation.

Select Add to VCC on the official download page. Confirm the repository in VCC and open Manage Project for your project. Add MingToon, open Unity, and wait for package import and compilation to finish. Use VCC's Manage Project for subsequent updates.

Download the installer .unitypackage from the official BOOTH product. Import it in Unity using Assets > Import Package > Custom Package. Stay connected to the internet while the DLL installer automatically installs the required MingToon package. No separate install button is needed for the first installation. On later Unity launches, the updater checks for a new version. Installation starts only when you select Update in the prompt. Skip applies to that version only. Restarting Unity does not automatically install an update.

Check Packages > MingToon in the Project window and the installation path Packages/com.studioraming.mingtoon. After Unity finishes importing and compiling, check the Console for errors and confirm that your materials display their MingToon shaders correctly. Ming Light Controller is a separate package. Install or update MLC separately if you use it. This MingToon release contains the BRP core and does not include the URP add-on.

If you upgraded a project from an earlier version, perform the following two steps once each. 1. Run schema migration once Tools > Studio Raming > MingToon > Advanced > Migrate Project To Current Schema Material schema has moved from version 10 to 11. Two new toggles were added: Enable Fresnel Rim Mask and Enable Rim Shade Mask. Old materials do not have these toggles, so they read as disabled. Migration finds masks that are not the default white and enables the toggles. Rim masks do not apply to materials until you run this. Materials with default white masks remain disabled, which is fine. Migration confirms before running and backs up changed files. When complete, the console reports the count of processed materials, presets, and animation clips in one line, along with the backup path. → Rim 2. Bake cache regenerates Generated-shader cache version moves from 28 to 38, invalidating existing bake output. The next build or upload regenerates it automatically, so nothing needs manual deletion, but that one run takes longer. VRChat avatars must be re-uploaded for this version's fixes to take effect. Shaders are bundled in the avatar asset bundle, so already-uploaded avatars continue using the old shader. → VRChat

After script reload, Console must show this line: [MingToon] VRChat build hook compiled and registered. If this line is missing VRChat build hook does not exist. Upload will not trigger automatic optimization or VRChat-specific upload processing. Check: Is Unity version 2022.3.22f1? Is VRChat SDK3 properly imported into the project? (VRC_SDK_VRCSDK3 define)

From the menu, run Tools > Studio Raming > MingToon > Validate Project. Mainly checks whether the current build target satisfies Shader Model 4.5. If not, it reports an error, and materials will render magenta. → Support environment Supported editor streams are both 2021.3 and 2022.3 Neither will raise MING-ENV-UNITY-VERSION error. However, if VRC SDK is present but editor is 2021.3, the MING-VRC-UNITY-VERSION warning appears — "MingToon's VRChat integration compiles only on the 2022.3 stream, so this project has no avatar upload support." This is an accurate warning; if targeting VRChat, switch to 2022.3.22f1.

Project Shader Built-in Render Pipeline (BRP) — includes VRChat·Warudo StudioRaming/MingToon/BRP URP 12.x (Unity 2021.3) MingToon URP shader URP is not a VRChat target VRChat + URP is not supported. URP targets only Unity 2021.3 + URP 12.x. URP 13 and above, even if they appear to work, are not considered supported.

MingToon works completely without PPv2. All PPv2-related source is excluded by UNITY_POST_PROCESSING_STACK_V2 symbol, so a clean project needs no com.unity.postprocessing. To enable PPv2 integration: Install PPv2 3.4.0. Player Settings > Scripting Define Symbols, directly add UNITY_POST_PROCESSING_STACK_V2. Wait for Unity to recompile. Run Tools > Studio Raming > MingToon > Create or Repair BRP PPv2 Global Volume. note Installing the package alone does not create this symbol. Skipping step 2 means the menu does nothing. VRChat avatars inherit world post-processing, so PPv2 is mainly for scene preview·capture.
First Material · Troubleshooting

Purpose: Understand the boundary between the MingToon core and optional authoring or runtime tools. MingToon shaders and inspector work without an add-on; a locked button is an integration point for the corresponding tool.

Tool Integration visible from MingToon What still works without it Mask Maker MM buttons on supported mask slots and some vertex-paint launchers Assign mask textures and vertex colors made elsewhere Face SDF Studio Face SDF authoring and preview entry points Assign an existing Face SDF texture and use face shading Ming Light Controller Master Adjust / virtual-light entry points and avatar menu configuration Tune MingToon materials and use the core build and bake features This table describes the integration shape in the current source. The source does not establish each tool's public version, price, or distribution status. Face SDF Studio is currently unreleased, so these docs do not make its purchase or installation a prerequisite.

If you installed an add-on, wait for Unity compilation and reopen the inspector. Check whether the integration button is enabled. If it remains locked, check Console errors, the bridge API load state, the selected target, and the slot. Without an add-on, use the slot's texture and value fields instead of the locked button. MingToon discovers optional integrations through their bridge surface rather than a fixed compile-time assembly dependency. A missing bridge therefore does not by itself mean that the core shader failed to install or compile.

After starting with Manager, select the converted material you want to refine. Keep MingToon Manager on the avatar root. This guide follows the current inspector's surface, colour, and lighting controls. Check your installed version if names differ. Update VCC installations through VCC.

Desired change Open first Main controls Darker or brighter appearance Lighting → Core Light Response / Lighting Brightness Limits Lit Brightness · Indirect Light Lift · Minimum/Maximum Final Brightness Excessive world-light colour Lighting → Core Light Response Environment Color Influence · Preserve Base Map Color Texture colour Detail Maps → Surface Maps Base HSVG · Hue Rotation Space · Base Tint Cutout or transparency Surface Rendering / Alpha & Cutout Surface Mode · Base Map Opacity · Alpha Cutoff Backfaces and overlapping cloth Surface Rendering Visible Faces · Two-Sided Dual Pass Contribute as a depth occluder Surface Rendering Camera Depth Contribution Start with Quick Settings, then search or open Full Setup for individual controls. Face, Skin, and Common can be assigned at the top of the material inspector in release builds too. Editing a role or value with multiple materials selected applies it to all selected targets.
documents.s: Find the control for your change

documents.t: Start with the four controls in Core Light Response. Control Changes Starting point Lit Brightness Brightness multiplier on the lit side 1 is neutral; watch for highlights losing colour as it increases Environment Color Influence Light-probe and ambient hue Lower it when environment colour overwhelms skin or clothing; independent of brightness Indirect Light Lift How indirect light lifts dark areas 0 adds no indirect brightness; 1 uses its authored strength Preserve Base Map Color Lighting hue mixed into the completed base colour Higher favours base colour; does not preserve or increase brightness For overly dark areas, check Indirect Light Lift and Lighting Brightness Limits → Minimum Final Brightness. For washed-out bright areas, adjust Lit Brightness and Maximum Final Brightness. Preserve Base Map Color alone does not solve insufficient brightness. Use Additional Light Reception for point and spot light influence. Advanced settings expose more colour and response-curve controls. → Light and Shadow

Use Surface Maps for the base texture and colour adjustments. For a converted material, check existing assignments before replacing textures. Control Purpose Base Map Original surface texture Base HSVG Hue, saturation, value, and gamma adjustment Hue Rotation Space HSV or OKLab. Keep HSV when preserving a look authored with it Base Tint · Tint Blend Mode Multiply keeps texture shading; Normal replaces it with the selected colour Base Map Opacity Multiplies final base alpha; surface opacity independent of tint strength The older description of tint opacity does not describe the current Base Map Opacity control. Tint Blend Strength is an advanced compatibility setting for colour blending; it does not change final surface alpha. To show transparency, also choose the appropriate surface mode below.

Enable Gradation LUT and assign a horizontal ramp to remap the base colour per channel. Import the LUT as sRGB and use Gradation Strength for its contribution. Begin with HSVG and tint, adding a LUT when needed.

Enable Color Adjust Mask → Use Color Adjust Mask and assign the mask. White applies adjustment, black retains the original colour, and gray blends between them. Select a channel for a packed texture and invert when needed. The mask has its own tiling and offset. Do not assume changing Base Map tiling also aligns the mask; check the intended regions, such as eyes or skin.
documents.s: Limit colour adjustment to a region

documents.t: If the converted appearance already behaves as intended, there is no need to change its mode first. Choose by opacity, cutout, and overlapping-layer needs. Surface Rendering and Alpha & Cutout edit the same mode value. Current label Use Depth and overlap Opaque (2000) Ordinary skin and clothing Writes depth without alpha blending Cutout (2450) Cut edges in hair or eyelashes Discards pixels below Alpha Cutoff; the rest write depth Semi-Transparent (2499) Alpha blending where the nearest surface should win Writes depth in a camera-depth eligible queue; different from showing every overlapping layer through the others Transparent (3000) Layered cloth or glass that should show surfaces behind it The default colour pass writes no depth and uses transparent ordering; not a normal camera-depth-effect target The old transparent-with-outline-depth label is now Semi-Transparent (2499). Both transparent modes can retain outlines. Mode changes align render state, default queue, and outline-buffer state while preserving Alpha Cutoff and outline enable/appearance settings. Choosing Semi-Transparent does not guarantee every depth effect. Check camera-depth availability, Camera Depth Contribution, enabled modules, and the actual render queue. → Depth Effects

This decides whether other materials' 2D shadows, SSAO, and 2D rim read this material as an occluder. Turning it off excludes that contribution; normal colour rendering and real-time light shadows remain separate. The checkbox does not itself prepare the camera's depth texture.

Choose front faces, backfaces, two-sided rendering, or the two-sided/outline-flip combination under Visible Faces. Use two-sided rendering for cloth that must show both sides. Check Flip Backface Lighting Normal when its backface lighting looks wrong. Advanced Color Buffer → Two-Sided Dual Pass draws a two-sided surface's backfaces separately first. Consider it for folded-cloth overlap issues; it adds a pass, so apply it where needed.

First choose between the depth priority of Semi-Transparent (2499) and layer blending of Transparent (3000). The latter exposes Transparent Depth Prepass under Advanced Color Buffer. This relates to transparent sorting and outlines; it is distinct from Camera Depth Contribution and real-time light shadows. Do not enable it indiscriminately for every overlap problem.

Check the Alpha & Cutout section master. For a separate transparency texture, enable Alpha Mask, set its texture, channel, inversion, and strength, then adjust Alpha Cutoff. Lower alpha does not turn Opaque mode into alpha blending. Alpha To Coverage depends on MSAA. If MSAA is disabled, repeatedly increasing its sharpness will not produce the expected edge smoothing. Camera Depth Alpha Cutoff, shown for semi-transparent/transparent modes, adjusts the depth silhouette separately from colour alpha. Open the distance, Fresnel, or directional alpha groups only when needed. Establish mask, surface opacity, and cutoff first.

Brightness/tint authoring rows in Master Adjust appear when MLC is installed; they are absent without it. Performance Distance works without an add-on and reduces sample limits and selected effects at distance. If an effect disappears far away, check its distance and scale settings. → Ming Light Controller

Normal maps control surface detail; occlusion maps affect indirect-light occlusion. Check module toggles and strength as well as texture assignments. Continue with normal layers, Matcap, emission, and PBR in Detail Maps. Render Disabled stops drawing the material. All Effects is the parent switch for stylized effects. Distinguish a missing material from an individual unresponsive effect.
Light and Shadow · Using the Inspector · Basic Settings Reference. After editing, keep Manager on the avatar root and continue with VRC SDK upload or WARUDO mod build.

Purpose: Apply one value to several MingToon materials, or save and reuse a look preset. The first action is to open Bulk Settings, choose a scope and filters, and check Preview Material Count. There are three tools: Tool Best for Bulk Settings panel Applying common values across a selected, Manager, or scene scope Material preset Saving and reusing a values-focused look Copy / Paste Moving one property, layer, or tab to compatible targets
Switch the inspector View to Bulk Settings. The panel first finds unique MingToon materials in the current scope, then shows common properties.

Control Choices and meaning Scope Selected Objects, MingToon Manager, Active Scene, Loaded Scenes Include Inactive Objects Includes disabled clothing and objects; default is on Material Kind All, Standard, Face Surface Kind All, Opaque, Cutout, Transparent For the MingToon Manager scope, Character Root is the Manager assigned to the avatar root; its child renderers are searched. For avatar or outfit editing, choose the Manager on the avatar root. The Face filter uses the material tag MingToonSurfaceKind=Face; Standard is the inverse. Surface filtering reads _MingSurfaceMode: 0=Opaque, 1=Cutout, and 2 or higher=Transparent.

Set the scope, inactive-object option, and filters. Read Preview Material Count. Press Refresh after changing clothing or scenes. Optionally press Select to put the result into the Unity selection. Open a Common Look group and edit a value. Only MingToon materials remain, and duplicates are included once. A multi-material edit is one Undo unit. Each row writes only to selected materials that declare that property, so a row can apply to part of the selection.

The panel currently has Base Lighting, Shadows, Stylization, and Outline / Emission groups. Base Lighting can include all effects, base tint, Base Map Opacity, output intensity/tint/saturation, color preservation, light color influence, brightness limits, normal strength, and smoothness. Shadow, style, outline, and emission properties appear only when the target shader declares them. Property Search matches the property name, displayed label, or registered aliases. Groups expand while searching. If there are no matches, clear the search or inspect the selected materials.

Save User Preset stores the current MingToon look as an asset. To apply one, choose a Factory or User preset from the dropdown and press Apply. For multiple targets, read the target count and scope before confirming an overwrite. The default capture and apply are values-focused. They store floats, colors, and vectors classified as look values by the current shader. Material render queue and other material-identity state are not written by a look preset. The panel's default preset keeps each target's textures. Only an explicitly requested texture capture stores and applies non-empty textures with their Tiling / Offset. Expand Capture Scope to save the whole material or selected tabs. An empty tab selection means the whole material. Shadow Color and Fresnel checkboxes decide whether those values are included on apply. Selecting a preset and pressing Apply are separate actions, and Apply can be undone.

Right-click a property or layer header for value, layer, and tab menus. Only compatible properties are written; a layer from another module or an incompatible value type is skipped. Check applied/skipped counts in the Console log. See Common Texture Slot UI for the menu list.

If the preview count is zero, check scope, the avatar-root Manager, Include Inactive, and the Face/Surface filters in that order. If a row is absent, check whether at least one selected material declares that property. If a change is not visible, check the mixed-value state, the module enable toggle, layer count, and strength. If a preset does not apply, check the selected preset, target count, and any schema error dialog.
